📝 Domain 1: Tokens & Policies (Questions 1-14)

Q1Which token type is NOT persisted to storage and thus cannot be renewed or looked up after creation?
A. Service token
B. Periodic token
C. Batch token
D. Orphan token
Answer: C. Batch tokens are lightweight, not stored in Vault's storage backend, cannot be renewed, revoked individually, or looked up. Service tokens (A) are the default and are stored. Periodic (B) and Orphan (D) tokens are types of service tokens.
Q2What HCL capability is required to list keys under a KV v2 path?
A. read
B. list
C. enumerate
D. browse
Answer: B. The list capability allows listing keys. read (A) allows reading individual secrets. Note: for KV v2, you need path "secret/metadata/*" { capabilities = ["list"] } to list keys.
Q3A token was created with -ttl=2h and -period=24h. Its parent token is revoked after 1 hour. What happens to this token?
A. It is revoked immediately (child follows parent)
B. It continues until its TTL expires (it is periodic, so it's orphaned)
C. It continues until its period expires
D. It becomes a root token
Answer: B. A periodic token (created with -period) is automatically an orphan — it has no parent. Revoking its "parent" doesn't affect it. It lives as long as it's renewed within each period.
Q4Which policy grants access to ALL paths and ALL capabilities?
A. path "+" { capabilities = ["*"] }
B. path "*" { capabilities = ["root"] }
C. path "*" { capabilities = ["create","read","update","delete","list","sudo"] }
D. There is no policy equivalent — only the root token has full access
Answer: C. path "*" matches all paths, and ["create","read","update","delete","list","sudo"] covers all capabilities. Option A uses "*" for capabilities which is valid shorthand. Option B is wrong — "root" is not a capability. Option D is wrong — you CAN create admin-equivalent policies.
Q5What command shows which capabilities a token has on a specific path?
A. vault token lookup
B. vault token capabilities <token> <path>
C. vault policy check <token> <path>
D. vault token verify <token> <path>
Answer: B. vault token capabilities evaluates policies attached to a token and returns the effective capabilities for a given path. vault token lookup (A) shows metadata but not path-specific capabilities.
Q6What is response wrapping used for?
A. Compressing API responses for faster transmission
B. Encrypting a secret so only a specific token can unwrap it — single-use delivery
C. Bundling multiple API responses into one HTTP response
D. Wrapping audit logs in TLS for secure transmission
Answer: B. Response wrapping creates a single-use token (wrap token) that contains the original response. Anyone with the wrapping token can unwrap it ONCE to get the original data. Used for secure secret delivery in CI/CD pipelines.
Q7A policy has path "secret/data/app/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }. Can a token with this policy read secret/data/app/config?
A. Yes — * matches any single path segment
B. No — * in the path does not span slashes (it's not a glob)
C. Yes — * matches everything including slashes
D. No — * only matches at the end of a path
Answer: B. In Vault policy paths, * does NOT span /. secret/data/app/* matches secret/data/app/foo but NOT secret/data/app/config (no deeper nesting). For recursive matching, use secret/data/app/** or secret/data/app/* only matches one level.
Q8What happens to a service token's child tokens when the parent token expires?
A. Child tokens continue unaffected
B. All child tokens are immediately revoked
C. Child tokens become root tokens
D. Child tokens are revoked after their own TTL expires
Answer: B. Service tokens form a parent-child tree. When a parent is revoked or expires, ALL descendants are recursively revoked. This is the "tree revocation" principle. Orphan tokens break this chain.
Q9Which capability allows a token to perform root-protected operations like mounting engines?
A. root
B. admin
C. sudo
D. super
Answer: C. sudo capability grants access to root-protected paths (like sys/mounts, sys/auth, sys/policy). There is no "root" or "admin" or "super" capability. sudo is the special one.
Q10What is the difference between default_lease_ttl and max_lease_ttl in Vault configuration?
A. They are the same — both set the maximum TTL
B. default_lease_ttl is the TTL if none is specified; max_lease_ttl is the absolute ceiling
C. default_lease_ttl is for tokens; max_lease_ttl is for secrets
D. default_lease_ttl applies to tokens; max_lease_ttl applies to leases
Answer: B. default_lease_ttl is applied when no TTL is explicitly requested. max_lease_ttl is the hard limit — even if a role specifies 90d, it's capped at max_lease_ttl. Both apply to tokens AND secrets.

📝 Domain 2: Secrets Engines (Questions 11-22)

Q11What is the key difference between KV v1 and KV v2 secrets engines?
A. KV v1 supports dynamic secrets; KV v2 is static only
B. KV v2 supports versioning (10 versions by default); KV v1 does not
C. KV v1 uses /data/ prefix; KV v2 does not
D. KV v2 is only available in Enterprise
Answer: B. KV v2 supports versioning — every write creates a new version; old versions are retained (10 by default, configurable). KV v1 overwrites on write with no version history. KV v2 uses /data/ prefix (not v1). Both are in Community and Enterprise.
Q12To read a secret from KV v2 at path secret/myapp, which API path is correct?
A. vault read secret/myapp
B. vault kv get secret/myapp
C. vault kv get -version=1 secret/myapp
D. vault read secret/data/myapp
Answer: B. For KV v2, use vault kv get (the kv subcommand handles the /data/ prefix automatically). Option D would work as a raw API call. vault read secret/myapp (A) is KV v1 syntax.

📝 Mock Questions 13-22 (continued)

Q13What command permanently deletes a specific version of a KV v2 secret?
A. vault kv delete secret/myapp
B. vault kv destroy -versions=3 secret/myapp
C. vault kv metadata delete secret/myapp
D. vault delete secret/data/myapp
Answer: B. vault kv destroy -versions=N permanently removes a version. vault kv delete (A) soft-deletes (marks as deleted, recoverable). vault kv metadata delete (C) deletes ALL versions and metadata.
Q14To configure a database secrets engine, what is the correct order?
A. Create role → Configure connection → Issue credentials
B. Configure connection → Create role → Read credentials
C. Mount engine → Read credentials → Configure connection
D. Create role → Read credentials → Configure connection
Answer: B. The correct flow is: (1) Enable DB engine → (2) vault write database/config/<name> (connection) → (3) vault write database/roles/<role> (creation SQL) → (4) vault read database/creds/<role> (get dynamic credentials).
Q15Which PKI secret engine endpoint issues a new certificate?
A. pki/cert/new
B. pki/issue/<role>
C. pki/certs/<role>
D. pki/generate/<role>
Answer: B. pki/issue/<role> generates a new certificate based on the role's configuration (TTL, allowed domains, key type). The role must exist: vault write pki/roles/<role>.
Q16What does the Transit secrets engine provide?
A. Network-level TLS encryption between services
B. Encryption-as-a-Service — encrypt/decrypt data without storing it in Vault
C. Dynamic SSH key generation for Linux servers
D. Automatic secret rotation for all mounted engines
Answer: B. Transit is Encryption-as-a-Service. You send plaintext, Vault encrypts it and returns ciphertext. Vault stores ONLY the encryption key, not your data. Great for application-level encryption without managing crypto libraries.
Q17What is a dynamic secret?
A. A secret that changes its value automatically every hour
B. A secret generated on-demand with a lease — automatically revoked when the lease expires
C. A secret stored in multiple KV engines simultaneously
D. A secret that requires multi-factor authentication to read
Answer: B. Dynamic secrets are created on-demand (e.g., DB credentials, cloud IAM keys) with a lease TTL. When the lease expires (or is revoked), Vault automatically deletes the credential from the target system. This is Vault's killer feature.
Q18Which engine would you use to generate TOTP (Time-based One-Time Passwords) for MFA?
A. Transit engine
B. TOTP secrets engine
C. PKI engine
D. Transform engine
Answer: B. Vault has a built-in TOTP secrets engine. You create a key, and Vault generates TOTP codes (like Google Authenticator). Use it for MFA integration or generating one-time codes.
Q19What is the purpose of the vault lease renew command?
A. Extends the TTL of a dynamic secret or token lease
B. Creates a new lease for an existing secret
C. Transfers a lease from one token to another
D. Upgrades a short-lived lease to a permanent one
Answer: A. vault lease renew <lease_id> extends the TTL of a dynamic secret's lease (or token) without generating a new credential. If you don't renew before TTL expires, the secret is revoked.
Q20What is the default number of versions kept in KV v2?
A. 1
B. 5
C. 10
D. Unlimited
Answer: C. KV v2 keeps 10 versions by default. This is configurable per-mount: vault secrets tune -max-versions=20 secret/. Oldest versions are automatically deleted when the limit is exceeded.
Q21You need to give an application read-only access to a specific KV secret. Which policy is most restrictive while still working?
A. path "secret/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
B. path "secret/data/app/config" { capabilities = ["read"] }
C. path "secret/data/app/*" { capabilities = ["read","list"] }
D. path "*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
Answer: B. Specifying the exact path is most restrictive (least privilege). Option A grants read to all secrets under secret/. Option C grants read+list to the app tree. Option D is extremely dangerous — read access to everything.
Q22How do you check the current seal status of Vault?
A. vault operator seal
B. vault status
C. vault operator unseal
D. vault read sys/seal-status
Answer: B. vault status shows: Sealed (true/false), Key Shares, Key Threshold, Unseal Progress, and Version. vault operator seal (A) seals Vault; vault operator unseal (C) provides an unseal key.

📝 Domain 3: Auth Methods (Questions 23-32)

Q23What two pieces of information are required for AppRole authentication?
A. Username and password
B. RoleID and SecretID
C. Client certificate and private key
D. JWT token and Kubernetes SA
Answer: B. AppRole uses RoleID (like a username — not secret) and SecretID (like a password — secret, single-use or TTL-bound). Both are required to login: vault write auth/approle/login role_id=... secret_id=....
Q24When a Kubernetes pod authenticates to Vault, what does Vault validate?
A. The pod's environment variables
B. The ServiceAccount JWT token against the Kubernetes TokenReview API
C. The pod's IP address against a whitelist
D. The container image signature
Answer: B. Kubernetes auth works by: the pod sends its SA JWT to Vault, Vault calls the K8s TokenReview API to validate it, then checks if the SA name/namespace match the configured role. No credentials stored in Vault.
Q25What is an Identity Entity in Vault?
A. A Kubernetes ServiceAccount mapped to Vault
B. A unified representation of a user/application across multiple auth methods
C. A token with identity-based policies
D. An LDAP group imported into Vault
Answer: B. An Identity Entity represents one user or application, regardless of how they authenticated (AppRole, OIDC, K8s, etc.). Aliases from different auth methods are merged into one entity, enabling unified policy management.
Q26Which auth method would you use for human operators to login with their corporate Google Workspace accounts?
A. AppRole
B. Kubernetes
C. OIDC
D. TLS Certificate
Answer: C. OIDC (OpenID Connect) integrates with identity providers like Google Workspace, Okta, Azure AD. Users login via browser, get redirected through their IdP, and Vault receives verified identity claims.
Q27How do you enable the Kubernetes auth method at path kubernetes?
A. vault auth enable kubernetes
B. vault secrets enable kubernetes
C. vault auth enable -path=kubernetes kubernetes
D. vault write auth/kubernetes enable=true
Answer: A. vault auth enable kubernetes enables it at the default path kubernetes/. Option C also works but is redundant (default path matches the type). vault secrets enable (B) is for secrets engines, not auth methods.
Q28What is an Identity Group alias used for?
A. Creating an alternate name for a Vault namespace
B. Mapping an external group (e.g., LDAP group, OIDC group claim) to a Vault Identity Group
C. Creating a backup copy of a group for DR
D. Allowing a group to access multiple namespaces
Answer: B. Group aliases map external groups to internal Vault Identity Groups. When a user authenticates via OIDC and has group="engineering" in their claims, Vault maps them to the internal "eng-team" group with its policies.

📝 Mock Questions 29-40 — Auth, Architecture & Ops

Q29What is the correct order to configure a database secrets engine?
A. Create role → Configure connection → Issue credentials
B. Configure connection → Create role → Read credentials
C. Mount engine → Issue credentials → Configure connection
D. Create role → Read credentials → Configure connection
Answer: B. Enable engine → configure connection (database/config/...) → create role with creation SQL → read credentials (database/creds/...).
Q30What is Shamir's Secret Sharing used for in Vault?
A. Encrypting secrets before storage
B. Splitting the unseal key into shards — requires threshold to reconstruct
C. Distributing tokens across clusters
D. Sharing policies across namespaces
Answer: B. Shamir (e.g., 3/5) ensures no single admin can unseal Vault alone — key shares are distributed to different people.
Q31What is the difference between sealed and unsealed states?
A. Sealed: offline; Unsealed: online
B. Sealed: master key not in memory, can't decrypt; Unsealed: master key loaded, Vault operational
C. Sealed: no auth; Unsealed: auth works
D. Sealed: root-only; Unsealed: public access
Answer: B. When sealed, Vault's master key is cleared from memory — almost all operations fail. Unsealing loads the key into memory.
Q32What is the default/recommended storage backend since Vault 1.4?
A. Consul
B. Etcd
C. Integrated Raft
D. File system
Answer: C. Integrated Raft provides HA via leader election and log replication without external dependencies.
Q33Command to create a Raft snapshot?
A. vault operator backup
B. vault operator raft snapshot save backup.snap
C. vault snapshot create
D. vault operator raft backup
Answer: B. Snapshots compact the Raft log and serve as recovery points. Take every 6h in production.
Q34What does enabling a file audit device do?
A. Backs up Vault to a file
B. Logs all API requests/responses (with sensitive data HMAC'd) to a file
C. Records only errors to a file
D. Exports metrics to a file
Answer: B. Audit devices are append-only and tamper-proof. If all fail, Vault HALT — always have at least one file device.
Q35What is the Vault telemetry endpoint for Prometheus?
A. /v1/sys/audit
B. /v1/sys/metrics?format=prometheus
C. /v1/sys/health
D. /v1/sys/stats
Answer: B. No authentication required. Exposes RPS, latency, token count, seal status for Prometheus scraping and Grafana dashboards.

📝 Mock Questions 36-50 — Advanced Mixed Topics

Q36Correct policy path for reading KV v2 secret/app/config?
A. path "secret/app/config" { capabilities = ["read"] }
B. path "secret/data/app/config" { capabilities = ["read"] }
C. path "secret/app/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
D. path "secret/metadata/app/config" { capabilities = ["read"] }
Answer: B. KV v2 uses /data/ prefix for data operations. /metadata/ is for metadata. * doesn't span slashes.
Q37What happens if ALL audit devices fail (disk full + socket down)?
A. Vault continues without logging
B. Vault creates in-memory audit
C. Vault STOPS ALL requests — refuses unlogged operations
D. Vault disables failed devices and alerts
Answer: C. This is a security feature — Vault won't process requests without audit logging. Always maintain at least 2 devices.
Q38Which component encrypts all data before storage?
A. Audit device
B. Storage backend
C. Cryptographic barrier
D. Auth method
Answer: C. The barrier encrypts/decrypts data between Vault core and storage. Storage only sees ciphertext.
Q39Vault Agent templates render secrets into what?
A. Vault policies
B. Config files on disk using Go templates — auto-updated when secrets change
C. Terraform HCL
D. Audit log formats
Answer: B. Agent templates render secrets into files (e.g., database.yml) and watch for changes — the core of Vault on Kubernetes.
Q40What does the Vault CSI provider do?
A. Creates cloud storage for backups
B. Mounts Vault secrets as Kubernetes volumes via Container Storage Interface
C. Provides compute for plugins
D. Integrates with cloud IAM
Answer: B. Alternative to Agent sidecar — secrets appear as mounted files in pods via Kubernetes CSI.
Q41HA with Integrated Raft requires how many nodes minimum?
A. 1
B. 2
C. 3
D. 5
Answer: C. 3 nodes minimum for quorum (floor(3/2)+1=2). Always use odd numbers. 2 nodes can't form quorum if 1 fails.
Q42What does deny capability do in a policy?
A. Nothing — Vault is allow-only
B. Explicitly blocks access — overrides any allow from other policies
C. Suspends tokens temporarily
D. Denies only writes
Answer: B. deny takes precedence over allow. If any policy has deny on a path, access is blocked regardless of other policies.
Q43Init with -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=3. How many keys needed to unseal?
A. 1
B. 3
C. 5
D. Any number
Answer: B. Any 3 of 5 shares can reconstruct the master key. 2 shares can be lost without impact.
Q44What does vault operator seal do?
A. Locks Vault — master key cleared from memory, all operations stop
B. Re-encrypts all secrets
C. Locks one engine
D. Creates backup seal
Answer: A. Emergency lockdown — clears master key from memory. All API operations fail until unsealed again.
Q45Best way to inject Vault secrets into a Kubernetes pod?
A. Hardcode VAULT_TOKEN in Dockerfile
B. Vault Agent Injector sidecar with pod annotations
C. Store in Kubernetes Secrets
D. SSH into pod and create files
Answer: B. Mutating webhook injects Agent sidecar. Pod annotations specify secret paths and templates. Secrets never touch K8s Secrets.
Q46Pod annotated with vault.hashicorp.com/role: "jobpost". What must exist in Vault?
A. Policy named "jobpost"
B. K8s auth role "jobpost" mapping SA namespace/name to policies
C. AppRole with role_id "jobpost"
D. KV path named "jobpost"
Answer: B. vault write auth/kubernetes/role/jobpost bound_service_account_names=... token_policies=...
Q47Recommended Raft snapshot frequency in production?
A. Monthly
B. Every 6 hours
C. Before upgrades only
D. Daily
Answer: B. Every 6 hours compacts Raft log and provides recovery points. Automate via CronJob or systemd timer.
Q48Community vs Enterprise — key Enterprise-only features?
A. Rate limiting
B. Namespaces, DR/Perf Replication, HSM, Sentinel, MFA
C. KV v2 secrets
D. Raft storage
Answer: B. Enterprise adds multi-tenancy, replication, HSM support, policy-as-code (Sentinel), and MFA. Community has all core engines and auth methods.
Q49Critical metric for "Vault is sealed" alert?
A. vault_core_requests_total
B. vault_core_unsealed (0=sealed, 1=unsealed)
C. vault_runtime_alloc_bytes
D. vault_token_count
Answer: B. Alert on vault_core_unsealed != 1. This is your #1 critical alert — when sealed, ALL operations fail.
Q50What Vault feature securely delivers initial secrets to CI/CD without embedding long-lived credentials?
A. KV v2 versioning
B. Response wrapping — single-use wrap token containing the secret
C. Periodic tokens
D. Batch tokens
Answer: B. Response wrapping creates a one-time-use token. CI/CD unwraps it once to get the secret, then the wrapping token is consumed. Perfect for bootstrap/bootstrap scenarios.

27.5 Bridge to Vault Operations Professional

🚀 Associate → Ops Pro: Your Next Step

The Vault Operations Professional cert proves you can operate Vault at scale. This guide covers ~40% of Ops Pro topics (Ch 17-19 Ops, Ch 20-21 Encryption, Ch 22-23 Monitoring, Ch 25 Hardening). You're well-positioned.

📊 Associate vs Ops Pro
AreaAssociateOps Pro Adds
HA/DRBasic Raft, snapshotsMulti-site DR, Perf Replication, failover testing
Hardening15-point checklistFIPS 140-2, SELinux, HSM, Sentinel EGP
PerformanceListener/storage tuningLoad testing, capacity planning, perf replication
MonitoringTelemetry, PrometheusSLO/SLI, alert routing, log aggregation
UpgradesRolling upgradesZero-downtime, canary, rollback
🛠️ anihpj/jobpost — Associate to Ops Pro Bridge Scenario

As an Associate, you configured Vault for anihpj/jobpost on a single Kubernetes cluster: K8s auth, Vault Agent sidecar, KV v2 for app config, dynamic DB credentials for PostgreSQL.

As an Ops Pro, you would level up:

  • HA: Deploy a 3-node Vault Raft cluster across 3 availability zones. Configure anti-affinity so nodes run on different hosts. Test leader election by killing the active pod.
  • DR: Set up a DR secondary cluster in a different region. Ship Raft snapshots to S3 every 6 hours. Run a quarterly DR drill: promote secondary to primary and verify jobpost can still fetch secrets.
  • Zero-downtime upgrades: Upgrade Vault from 1.15 to 1.16 on a 3-node cluster one node at a time. Verify the cluster stays healthy (quorum maintained) throughout. Roll back if any node fails.
  • Sentinel EGP: Write a Sentinel policy that prevents jobpost from being deployed with a TTL longer than 30 days — enforcing organizational security policy at the Vault level, not just ACL.
  • SLO monitoring: Define SLO: "99.9% of Vault API requests complete in under 100ms." Build Grafana dashboards tracking this. Alert when error budget burn rate exceeds threshold.

This is the Ops Pro mindset: Associate = "I can configure Vault correctly." Ops Pro = "I can ensure Vault stays correct under any failure scenario."

📝 Chapter 27 — Mixed-Domain Exam Simulation

Q261What is the optimal way to handle 12 flagged questions with 10 minutes left?
A. ~50 sec each — don't get stuck, guess if uncertain
B. Skip all flagged
C. Pick "C" for all
D. Focus only on 3 easiest
Answer: A. ~50 sec/question. First instinct is usually right. Don't overthink flagged questions.
Q262Policy has path "secret/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }. Can it read secret/data/myapp?
A. Yes — * matches everything
B. No — * doesn't span /, need path "secret/data/*"
C. Yes — but only in KV v1
D. No — need sudo capability
Answer: B. In Vault policy paths, * does NOT match /. KV v2 uses /data/ prefix — must be in the policy path.
Q263Which Vault component auto-revokes expired DB credentials?
A. Audit device
B. Expiration manager
C. Storage backend
D. Auth method
Answer: B. The expiration manager tracks all leases and triggers revocation on TTL expiry.
Q264How to configure AWS KMS auto-unseal?
A. VAULT_SEAL_TYPE=awskms env var
B. seal "awskms" { ... } stanza in vault-config.hcl
C. vault operator unseal -method=awskms
D. Enable AWS engine and link to seal
Answer: B. Auto-unseal uses a seal stanza. Vault decrypts master key via KMS at startup — no manual unseal needed.
Q265Dev can't read secret/data/myapp with path "secret/*" { capabilities = ["read","list"] }. Why?
A. Need sudo capability
B. KV v2 needs /data/ prefix — path "secret/data/*"
C. Token expired
D. * doesn't match /data/
Answer: B and D are both correct. KV v2 uses /data/ prefix AND * doesn't span slashes. Fix: path "secret/data/*" { capabilities = ["read","list"] }.
Q266DR replication vs Performance replication?
A. Same thing — different names
B. DR: read-only standby (promotable). Perf: read-write secondary (forwards writes to primary)
C. DR: on-prem. Perf: cloud
D. DR: secrets only. Perf: policies only
Answer: B. DR is for disaster recovery (promotable standby). Performance replication is for geographic low-latency reads.
Q267Command for periodic orphan service token: TTL 72h, period 24h?
A. vault token create -ttl=72h -period=24h
B. vault token create -period=24h -explicit-max-ttl=72h
C. vault token create -ttl=72h -period=24h -orphan
D. vault token create -period=24h (periodic=auto-orphan)
Answer: B. Periodic tokens are automatically orphans. -explicit-max-ttl=72h sets hard expiration after 72h.
Q268Endpoint to check if standby node is healthy (K8s readiness probe)?
A. /v1/sys/health
B. /v1/sys/health?standbyok=true
C. /v1/sys/seal-status
D. /v1/sys/metrics
Answer: B. Without standbyok=true, standby returns 429. With it, standby returns 200 (ready).
Q2695-node Raft cluster — how many can fail before losing quorum?
A. 0
B. 2
C. 3
D. 4
Answer: B. Quorum = floor(5/2)+1 = 3. 2 can fail. Always use odd numbers of nodes.
Q270After Vault Associate, what's the NEXT certification?
A. Vault Advanced Developer
B. Vault Operations Professional
C. Vault Security Specialist
D. HashiCorp Certified: Vault Architect
Answer: B. Ops Pro → then Authorship (custom plugin development).

📝 A.2 — Detailed Explanations with Code, YAML & Diagrams

The 40 most commonly missed questions, explained with working code snippets, CLI output, YAML manifests, and ASCII diagrams. These are the questions that separate passing from failing.

🎫 Domain 1: Tokens & Policies (28%) — Trickiest Questions

Q46-Q50: Token Types Comparison
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         TOKEN TYPE DECISION TREE             │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Need lightweight, high-volume?               │
│   YES → Batch Token (encrypted blob)         │
│   NO  ↓                                      │
│ Need long-running service with auto-renew?   │
│   YES → Periodic Token (auto-orphaned)       │
│   NO  ↓                                      │
│ Don't want parent revoke to kill child?      │
│   YES → Orphan Token                         │
│   NO  → Service Token (default)              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q46: Service token — stored, renewable, revocable
vault token create -policy=app-read -ttl=1h

# Q47: Batch token — NOT stored, NOT renewable
vault token create -type=batch -policy=app-read

# Q48: Orphan — no parent
vault token create -orphan -policy=app-read

# Q49: Periodic — auto-renews forever
vault token create -period=24h -policy=svc-policy
Q56-Q60: Policy Capabilities & KV v2 Paths
# Q56: All capabilities
path "secret/data/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update","delete","list"]
}

# Q57: list needed to list keys
path "secret/metadata/*" {
  capabilities = ["list"]  # list ONLY, no read
}

# Q59: deny ALWAYS wins
path "secret/data/sensitive" {
  capabilities = ["deny"]  # Overrides ANY allow
}

# Q60: KV v2 REQUIRES /data/ prefix
path "secret/*" {           # ❌ WRONG for KV v2
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "secret/data/*" {      # ✅ CORRECT for KV v2
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

💡 Exam Trap: A policy for secret/* does NOT grant access to secret/data/* in KV v2. The * wildcard doesn't span slashes!

Q51-Q55: Response Wrapping Flow
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│       RESPONSE WRAPPING FLOW                 │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Vault ──(wrap-ttl=5m)──► Wrap Token          │
│   │                        │                 │
│   │                 App receives token        │
│   │                        │                 │
│   │              vault unwrap <token>        │
│   │                        │                 │
│   ◄──(unwrap)── Secret ◄───┘                 │
│                                              │
│ Token consumed — CANNOT unwrap again!        │
│ If intercepted, intended user knows.         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q51: Create wrapped AppRole SecretID
vault write -wrap-ttl=5m \
  auth/approle/role/anihpj-app/secret-id

# Q52: Unwrap (consumes the token)
vault unwrap hvs.CAESI...

# Q53: Create token with wrapping
vault token create -wrap-ttl=5m -policy=app-read
Q61-Q65: Templated Policies & Capabilities
# Q61: Dynamic path with entity name
path "secret/data/user/{{identity.entity.name}}/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update","delete"]
}
# Resolves to: secret/data/user/john-smith/*

# Q62: Check what a token can do
vault token capabilities hvs.CAESI... secret/data/app
# Output: ["read","list"]
# → Token can read and list, but NOT write

# Q63: Least privilege example
path "database/creds/anihpj-readonly" {
  capabilities = ["read"]  # Only read, no write
}
# NOT: path "database/creds/*" {capabilities=["*"]}

🔐 Domain 2: Secrets Engines (25%) — Trickiest Questions

Q16-Q20: KV v1 vs v2 — The /data/ Trap
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│        KV v2 PATH STRUCTURE                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  secret/                                     │
│  ├── data/app/db     ← Secret VALUES here    │
│  └── metadata/app/db ← Version INFO here     │
│                                              │
│  CLI: vault kv get secret/app/db             │
│  API: GET /v1/secret/data/app/db             │
│  Policy: path "secret/data/*" {...}          │
│                                              │
│  ⚠️ Policy MUST include /data/ for KV v2!    │
│  ⚠️ API MUST include /data/ for KV v2!       │
│  ✅ CLI handles /data/ automatically          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q16: KV v1 — simple, no versioning
vault secrets enable -version=1 kv

# Q17: KV v2 — versioned, /data/ prefix
vault secrets enable -version=2 kv

# Q19: Permanent destroy (KV v2 only)
vault kv destroy -versions=3 secret/app/db

# Q20: View version history
vault kv metadata get secret/app/db
Q21-Q25: Dynamic DB Secrets — Full Flow
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│    DYNAMIC DB SECRETS LIFECYCLE              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. vault write database/config/anihpj-pg    │
│     → Stores root DB creds in Vault          │
│                                              │
│  2. vault write database/roles/jobpost       │
│     → Defines: SQL, TTL=1h, MaxTTL=24h       │
│                                              │
│  3. vault read database/creds/jobpost        │
│     → Vault creates temp DB user             │
│     → Returns: username + password           │
│     → Lease created with TTL=1h              │
│                                              │
│  4. After TTL: Vault auto-deletes DB user    │
│     OR vault lease revoke <lease_id>         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q21: Correct order — config → role → creds
vault write database/config/anihpj-pg \
  plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \
  allowed_roles=jobpost-role \
  connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@..."

vault write database/roles/jobpost-role \
  db_name=anihpj-pg \
  creation_statements='CREATE USER "{{name}}" ...' \
  default_ttl=1h max_ttl=24h

vault read database/creds/jobpost-role
# Returns: username + password + lease_id
Q26-Q30: PKI, Transit, TOTP, SSH
# Q26: PKI — Issue certificate
vault write pki/issue/anihpj-dot-io \
  common_name=jobpost.anihpj.io ttl=720h

# Q27: Transit — Encrypt (Vault NEVER stores data)
BASE64=$(echo -n "credit-card-1234" | base64)
vault write transit/encrypt/payments \
  plaintext="$BASE64"
# Returns: ciphertext="vault:v1:ABC..."

# Q28: TOTP — Generate time-based code
vault read totp/code/jobpost-admin

# Q29: SSH — Sign client key
vault write ssh/sign/my-role \
  public_key=@$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa.pub
Q166-Q175: Transit Engine Deep Dive
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│       TRANSIT KEY ROTATION                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  v1 key: encrypts + decrypts                 │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼ rotate                                  │
│  v2 key: NEW encrypts, v1 STILL decrypts     │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼ rewrap (v1→v2)                          │
│  Old ciphertext → decrypt(v1) → encrypt(v2)  │
│  ALL inside Vault — plaintext never exposed  │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼ trim v1 (after all rewrap done)         │
│  Only v2 remains — v1 ciphertext lost!       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

🔑 Domain 3: Auth Methods (20%) — Trickiest Questions

Q31-Q35 + Q41-Q45: AppRole & K8s Auth
# Q31: AppRole — RoleID (public) + SecretID (secret)
vault write auth/approle/role/anihpj-app \
  token_policies=anihpj-app \
  secret_id_ttl=10m token_ttl=1h

# Get RoleID (not secret)
vault read auth/approle/role/anihpj-app/role-id

# Get SecretID (secret — use response wrapping!)
vault write -wrap-ttl=5m \
  auth/approle/role/anihpj-app/secret-id

# Q32: K8s auth — SA JWT via TokenReview
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/jobpost \
  bound_service_account_names=jobpost-sa \
  bound_service_account_namespaces=anihpj \
  policies=jobpost-k8s \
  ttl=1h

# Login from pod:
JWT=$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)
vault write auth/kubernetes/login role=jobpost jwt=$JWT
Q36-Q40: Identity — Entities, Groups, Aliases
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         IDENTITY SYSTEM                      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                              │
│  Entity: "john" (one person)                 │
│  ├── Alias: GitHub: john-gh                  │
│  ├── Alias: OIDC: john@corp.com              │
│  └── Alias: LDAP: CN=John,OU=Users           │
│                                              │
│  Group: "backend-team"                       │
│  ├── Entity: john                            │
│  ├── Entity: alice                           │
│  └── Policies: backend-policy                │
│                                              │
│  → john logs in via ANY method               │
│  → Vault merges to ONE entity                │
│  → Policies from "backend-team" group apply  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q39: Create entity
vault write identity/entity \
  name=john-dev \
  metadata=team=backend

# Q40: Create group with policies
vault write identity/group \
  name=backend-team \
  policies=backend-policy \
  member_entity_ids=<entity_id>

🏗️ Domain 4: Architecture (15%) — Trickiest Questions

Q6-Q10: Vault Architecture & Seal/Unseal
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│      VAULT REQUEST FLOW                      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Client                                      │
│    │  HTTPS + X-Vault-Token                  │
│    ▼                                         │
│  API (Parse + Validate TLS)                  │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼                                         │
│  Core (Token → Policy → Authorization)       │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼                                         │
│  Barrier (Encrypt data before storage)       │
│    │                                         │
│    ▼                                         │
│  Storage (Raft / Consul / Filesystem)        │
│                                              │
│  ⚠️ NO component can read plaintext secrets   │
│     after the barrier encrypts them.         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q8: Shamir — 5 shares, 3 threshold
vault operator init -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=3
# → 5 key shares, ANY 3 can unseal

# Q9: Raft — default storage backend
# vault-config.hcl:
storage "raft" {
  path = "/vault/data"
  node_id = "node-1"
}
# Q10: Request lifecycle
# Parse → TLS → Token → Policy → Barrier → Response
Q1-Q5: Why Vault? Core Concepts
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│     SECRET SPRAWL → VAULT SOLUTION           │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  BEFORE VAULT:                               │
│  • API keys in .env files                    │
│  • DB passwords in config maps               │
│  • SSH keys on every laptop                  │
│  • TLS certs expiring with no alert          │
│                                              │
│  AFTER VAULT (4 Pillars):                    │
│  • 🔒 STORE: Central encrypted storage       │
│  • 🔑 ACCESS: Fine-grained policies          │
│  • 📝 AUDIT: Every request logged            │
│  • 🔄 ROTATE: Auto-rotation + revocation     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

⚙️ Domain 5: Operations (12%) — Trickiest Questions

Q131-Q140: Raft Cluster Operations
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│     ROLLING UPGRADE WITH ZERO DOWNTIME       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. vault operator raft snapshot save s.snap │
│     ↓ (safety first!)                        │
│  2. Upgrade standby-1 → restart → unseal     │
│     Upgrade standby-2 → restart → unseal     │
│     ↓ (standbys done, active still running)  │
│  3. vault operator step-down <active-node>   │
│     ↓ (leader moves to upgraded standby)     │
│  4. Upgrade ex-leader → restart → unseal     │
│     ↓                                        │
│  ✅ All nodes upgraded, zero downtime!       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
# Q131: Correct upgrade order
vault operator raft snapshot save backup.snap
# Then: upgrade standbys first!
# Then: vault operator step-down
# Finally: upgrade ex-leader

# Q133: 2 of 3 fail = NO QUORUM
# Raft needs majority: 3/5 = 2 can fail
# With 3 nodes: 2 must survive (can lose 1)

# Q134: Add new node
vault operator raft join https://leader:8200

# Q136: Remove dead node
vault operator raft remove-peer node-3
Q121-Q130: Backup & Disaster Recovery
# Q121: Snapshot includes everything
vault operator raft snapshot save backup.snap
# Contains: secrets, policies, tokens, auth, config

# Q122: Restore procedure
# 1. Stop ALL Vault nodes
systemctl stop vault
# 2. Clear old data
rm -rf /vault/data/*
# 3. Restore snapshot
vault operator raft snapshot restore backup.snap
# 4. Start Vault
systemctl start vault
# 5. Unseal
vault operator unseal <key_share>

# Q124: Automated backup CronJob (K8s)
kubectl create cronjob vault-backup \
  --schedule="0 */6 * * *" \
  --image=vault:latest \
  -- vault operator raft snapshot save \
    /backup/vault-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M).snap
Q111-Q120: Day-to-Day Operations
# Q112: Unseal — submit key share
vault operator unseal <base64_key_share>
# Repeat until threshold met (progress: 1/3→2/3→3/3)

# Q113: Health check
curl $VAULT_ADDR/v1/sys/health
# 200 = active, 429 = standby, 501 = not init

# Q116: Critical metrics
vault_core_unsealed        # MUST = 1
vault_core_handle_request  # Request rate
vault_token_count          # Active tokens
vault_expire_num_leases    # Active leases

# Q117: 3 audit types
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault/audit.log
vault audit enable socket address=127.0.0.1:9090 socket_type=tcp
vault audit enable syslog tag=vault facility=LOCAL0
Q241-Q250: Performance & Production Hardening
# Q241: Storage is #1 bottleneck — Use SSD/NVMe
storage "raft" {
  path = "/vault/data"  # ← MUST be on SSD
}

# Q242: TLS minimum for production
listener "tcp" {
  tls_min_version = "tls12"
  tls_cert_file = "/etc/vault.d/cert.pem"
  tls_key_file  = "/etc/vault.d/key.pem"
}

# Q244: mlock prevents swap to disk
# /etc/systemd/system/vault.service:
[Service]
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_IPC_LOCK
LimitMEMLOCK=infinity

# Q246: Raft performance multiplier
storage "raft" {
  performance_multiplier = 1  # 0-10 range
}

Q66-Q75: Vault Agent Injector on K8s
# Q67-Q68: Deployment annotations for Agent injection
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jobpost
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
        vault.hashicorp.com/role: "jobpost"
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-db: |
          {{- with secret "database/creds/jobpost-role" -}}
          DB_USER={{ .Data.username }}
          DB_PASS={{ .Data.password }}
          {{- end }}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: jobpost-sa  # Q71: SA for K8s auth
      containers:
      - name: jobpost-app
        image: anihpj/jobpost:latest
Q86-Q95: VSO vs CSI vs Sidecar
# Q86: VSO — VaultStaticSecret CRD
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultStaticSecret
metadata:
  name: jobpost-db
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  vaultAuthRef: vault-auth
  mount: secret
  path: anihpj/db
  destination:
    name: jobpost-db-k8s  # → K8s Secret
    create: true
  refreshAfter: 1h

# Q89: CSI Driver — mount as volume
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-db
spec:
  provider: vault
  parameters:
    vaultAddress: "https://vault.vault:8200"
    objects: |
      - objectName: "db-creds"
        secretPath: "database/creds/jobpost-role"

⚡ Appendix M: 20 Critical Patterns — Cram Sheet

⚡ READ THIS BEFORE THE EXAM — These 20 patterns cover ~70% of questions
1. Init + Unseal

vault operator init -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=3
vault operator unseal <key> (3 times)
vault status → check Sealed: false

2. Enable KV v2

vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2
vault kv put secret/app key=val
vault kv get secret/app
⚠️ Policy must use /data/ prefix!

3. Dynamic DB Secrets

vault secrets enable database
vault write database/config/postgres ...
vault write database/roles/app-role ...
vault read database/creds/app-role

4. AppRole Auth

vault auth enable approle
vault write auth/approle/role/myrole token_policies=myapp
vault read auth/approle/role/myrole/role-id
vault write auth/approle/role/myrole/secret-id

5. K8s Auth

vault auth enable kubernetes
vault write auth/kubernetes/config kubernetes_host=...
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/app bound_service_account_names=app-sa bound_service_account_namespaces=default token_policies=app

6. Write a Policy

path "secret/data/app/*" { capabilities = ["read","list"] }
vault policy write app-policy app-policy.hcl
⚠️ * doesn't span / — use + for single segment

7. Token Creation

vault token create -policy=app (service)
vault token create -type=batch -policy=app (batch)
vault token create -period=24h (periodic, auto-orphan)
vault token create -orphan

8. Token Capabilities

vault token capabilities <token> secret/data/app
→ Returns: ["read","list"]
Tests what a token can actually DO on a path

9. PKI Cert Issuance

vault secrets enable pki
vault write pki/root/generate/internal common_name=...
vault write pki/roles/web-server ...
vault write pki/issue/web-server common_name=app.example.com

10. Transit Encrypt/Decrypt

vault secrets enable transit
vault write -f transit/keys/mykey
vault write transit/encrypt/mykey plaintext=$(echo -n "secret" | base64)
⚠️ Vault stores only the KEY, not your data!

11. Raft Snapshot

vault operator raft snapshot save backup.snap
vault operator raft snapshot restore backup.snap
⚠️ Take every 6 hours in production!

12. Audit Device

vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit.log
⚠️ If ALL audit devices fail → Vault STOPS
Always have ≥2 devices (file + socket)

13. Vault Agent Sidecar

Pod annotation: vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
vault.hashicorp.com/role: "app-role"
Agent auto-authenticates, fetches secrets, renders templates

14. Seal/Unseal States

Sealed: Master key NOT in memory → operations fail
Unsealed: Master key loaded → Vault operational
vault operator seal → emergency lockdown
Alert: vault_core_unsealed != 1

15. KV v2 Versioning

vault kv get -version=2 secret/app
vault kv destroy -versions=2 secret/app (permanent)
vault kv metadata get secret/app (version list)
Default: 10 versions retained, configurable

16. Lease Management

vault lease renew <lease_id>
vault lease revoke <lease_id>
vault lease lookup <lease_id>
Expiration manager auto-revokes expired leases

17. Response Wrapping

vault write -wrap-ttl=5m auth/approle/role/myrole/secret-id
vault unwrap <wrap_token>
Single-use! Perfect for CI/CD bootstrap

18. Identity System

vault write identity/entity name="john" policies="app"
vault write identity/group name="devs" member_entity_ids=... policies="dev"
Unified identity across auth methods

19. Health & Readiness

vault status → Sealed? Initialized?
curl /v1/sys/health?standbyok=true → 200=ready
K8s liveness: exec: ["vault","status"]
K8s readiness: httpGet: /v1/sys/health?standbyok=true

20. Namespaces (Enterprise)

vault namespace create engineering
VAULT_NAMESPACE=engineering/ vault secrets list
⚠️ Siblings CANNOT see each other
⚠️ Children CANNOT navigate up

📋 Appendix B: Top 50 Vault CLI Commands You MUST Know

These 50 commands cover 95% of what you'll type in the exam and in production. Each command includes syntax, description, a real example with the anihpj/jobpost project, and expected output. Memorize these before exam day.

🔧 Category 1: Server Operations (8 Commands)

vault status

Syntax: vault status
Description: Check seal state, initialization, HA status. Works even when sealed.
Example: vault status
Output: Sealed: false | Initialized: true | Version: 1.16.0

vault operator init

Syntax: vault operator init -key-shares=N -key-threshold=K
Description: Initialize Vault. Generates unseal keys + root token. Run ONCE per cluster.
Example: vault operator init -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=3
Output: 5 unseal keys (hex-encoded) + 1 root token

vault operator unseal

Syntax: vault operator unseal <key>
Description: Provide a Shamir key share. Repeat until threshold reached.
Example: vault operator unseal abc123... (run 3x for threshold=3)
Output: Sealed: true | Unseal Progress: 1/3 → finally Sealed: false

vault operator seal

Syntax: vault operator seal
Description: Emergency lockdown — wipes master key from memory. ALL operations stop.
Example: vault operator seal
Output: Success! Vault is sealed.

vault operator raft list-peers

Syntax: vault operator raft list-peers
Description: Show all Raft cluster nodes with their IDs, addresses, and voter status.
Example: vault operator raft list-peers
Output: Table of nodes: vault-0 (leader), vault-1 (follower), vault-2 (follower)

vault operator raft snapshot save

Syntax: vault operator raft snapshot save <file>
Description: Create point-in-time backup of ALL Vault data. Run every 6 hours.
Example: vault operator raft snapshot save /backups/vault-$(date +%Y%m%d).snap
Output: Snapshot saved to /backups/vault-20260613.snap

vault operator raft snapshot restore

Syntax: vault operator raft snapshot restore <file>
Description: Restore Vault from a snapshot. Requires stopping all nodes first.
Example: vault operator raft snapshot restore /backups/vault-20260613.snap
Output: Success! Restored snapshot. Then unseal to complete recovery.

vault operator step-down

Syntax: vault operator step-down
Description: Force current leader to become follower — triggers Raft leader election.
Example: vault operator step-down
Output: Success! Stepped down. New leader elected within seconds.

📝 Appendix C: Vault Policy Templates — Ready-to-Use

10 production-ready HCL policy templates with line-by-line explanations. Copy, paste, customize — each template follows least privilege and is built for the anihpj/jobpost project. All templates use KV v2 (with /data/ prefix) and follow exam-tested patterns.

Template 1: Read-Only Application (Least Privilege)

Policy HCL
# app-readonly.hcl
# Purpose: Read-only access to app config
# Use for: Monitoring tools, health checkers
path "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "secret/metadata/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["list"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Line 1-2: Comment — identifies the policy
🔹 Line 4-6: /data/ path grants read only — can view secrets but can't modify them. KV v2 requires /data/ prefix!
🔹 Line 7-9: /metadata/ path grants list — can see which secrets exist but not read values. Separating data from metadata is a v2 security feature.
🔹 Exam Note: list on /metadata/ is required for vault kv list to work!

Template 2: Application with Dynamic Database Credentials

Policy HCL
# app-with-db.hcl
# Purpose: Django app needs KV config + DB creds
# Use for: anihpj Django pods
path "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}
path "database/creds/jobpost-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Lines 4-6: read+list on KV — the app can both read secrets AND list available keys (needed for vault kv list)
🔹 Lines 7-9: read on DB creds path — generates dynamic PostgreSQL credentials. Note: read on database/creds/ TRIGGERS credential generation!
🔹 Security: App CANNOT delete secrets (no delete), CANNOT modify DB config (path limited to creds/), CANNOT create new roles

Template 3: Full Admin Policy

Policy HCL
# admin.hcl
# Purpose: Full administrative access
# Use for: Vault operators, SRE team
# ⚠️ DANGER: Equivalent to root in scope!
path "*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update",
                  "delete","list","sudo"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Lines 4-5: path "*" matches EVERY Vault path — secrets, auth, sys, identity, everything
🔹 Lines 5-7: All 6 capabilities including sudo for root-protected paths (mount engines, manage auth)
🔹 ⚠️ WARNING: Attach this only to operator tokens. NEVER to application tokens. Use token_num_uses to limit admin token usage
🔹 Better alternative: Split into separate policies for different admin responsibilities

Template 4: CI/CD Pipeline Policy

Policy HCL
# cicd-pipeline.hcl
# Purpose: CI/CD can create deploy tokens + read
#          build secrets + get deploy DB creds
path "auth/token/create" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
path "secret/data/build/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "database/creds/deploy-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Lines 4-6: auth/token/create with update — CI/CD can create deployment tokens. Restrict with allowed_parameters to prevent privilege escalation!
🔹 Lines 7-9: Read-only on build secrets — CI/CD can read env vars but not modify them
🔹 Lines 10-12: DB credentials for deployment — each deployment gets unique, short-lived DB access
🔹 Security note: Add token_bound_cidrs=10.0.0.0/8 to restrict CI/CD token usage to internal network

Template 5: Templated Per-User Policy (Identity-Based)

Policy HCL
# user-kv.hcl
# Purpose: ONE policy for ALL users —
#          each user gets their own KV namespace
# Requires: Identity entities with entity names
path "secret/data/user/{{identity.entity.name}}/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update",
                  "delete","list"]
}
path "secret/metadata/user/{{identity.entity.name}}/*" {
  capabilities = ["list"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Line 5: {{identity.entity.name}} — template variable resolves to the authenticated entity's name (e.g., "john-dev")
🔹 Result: John accesses secret/data/user/john-dev/*, Sarah accesses secret/data/user/sarah/* — same policy, different paths!
🔹 Lines 6-7: Full CRUD+list within their namespace
🔹 Lines 10-12: Metadata access for vault kv list
🔹 Exam Note: If entity has no name → template resolves to empty string → path matches nothing → DENIED

Template 6: Multi-Tenant Team Policy (Environment + Team Isolation)

Policy HCL
# team-policy.hcl
# Purpose: ONE policy for ALL teams & envs
# Requires: entity metadata: team + env
path "secret/data/{{identity.entity.metadata.env}}/{{identity.entity.metadata.team}}/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update","delete","list"]
}
path "database/creds/{{identity.entity.metadata.env}}-{{identity.entity.metadata.team}}-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
Line-by-Line Explanation

🔹 Line 5: {{identity.entity.metadata.env}} + {{identity.entity.metadata.team}} — double template for env+team isolation
🔹 Setup: vault write identity/entity name="alpha-dev" metadata='{"env":"dev","team":"alpha"}'
🔹 Result: Alpha-dev team accesses secret/data/dev/alpha/*, Beta-prod accesses secret/data/prod/beta/*
🔹 Lines 8-10: DB credentials follow same pattern — database/creds/dev-alpha-role
🔹 Security: Teams in different envs CANNOT see each other's secrets — enforced by template, not separate policies!

Template 7: Kubernetes Pod Policy (Vault Agent Pattern)

k8s-pod.hcl — For pods using Vault Agent Sidecar
# k8s-pod.hcl
# Purpose: K8s pod accessing secrets via Vault Agent
# Use with: auth/kubernetes/role binding
path "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "database/creds/jobpost-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
# Agent needs self-lookup and renewal (from default policy)
path "auth/token/lookup-self" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "auth/token/renew-self" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

Key Insight: If you set token_no_default_policy=true on the K8s auth role, you MUST include auth/token/lookup-self and auth/token/renew-self in this policy — otherwise the Agent can't manage its own token!

Template 8: Monitoring & Observability Read-Only

monitoring.hcl — For Prometheus, Grafana, health checkers
# monitoring.hcl
# Purpose: Read-only access for monitoring tools
# No secret access — metrics and health only!
path "sys/metrics" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "sys/health" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "sys/seal-status" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "sys/leader" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
# Optional: allow listing engines (know what exists)
path "sys/mounts" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

Security note: This policy grants ZERO access to secrets — only Vault's operational endpoints. Attach to a dedicated "monitoring" token with CIDR binding to the monitoring subnet.

Template 9: Sentinel EGP — Business Hours Only (Enterprise)

business-hours.sentinel — Allow access only 9am-5pm weekdays
# business-hours.sentinel
# Vault Enterprise only — Sentinel policy-as-code
import "time"

# Allow access only during business hours (Mon-Fri, 9am-5pm UTC)
main = rule {
    time.now.hour >= 9 and
    time.now.hour < 17 and
    time.now.weekday_name not in ["Saturday", "Sunday"]
}

# Override: allow admins anytime
admins_override = rule {
    identity.entity.metadata.role is "admin"
}

# Main policy: business hours OR admin override
main = rule {
    business_hours or admins_override
}

When to use Sentinel: When ACL policies can't express the condition — time-based, IP-based, or value-based access controls. Sentinel is Enterprise-only. For the Associate exam, know that Sentinel EXISTS but ACL policies are what you write.

Template 10: anihpj/jobpost Complete Production Policy Set

anihpj-complete.hcl — All-in-one application policy
# anihpj-jobpost.hcl — Complete policy for jobpost Django app
# ============================================
# SECTION 1: KV v2 — Application Configuration
# ============================================
path "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "secret/metadata/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["list"]
}

# ============================================
# SECTION 2: Dynamic DB — PostgreSQL Credentials
# ============================================
path "database/creds/jobpost-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
# NOTE: "read" on database/creds/ TRIGGERS
# credential generation! Each read = new DB user.

# ============================================
# SECTION 3: Transit — App-Level Encryption
# ============================================
# Encrypt sensitive user data (PII) before DB storage
path "transit/encrypt/jobpost-key" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
# Decrypt when reading from DB
path "transit/decrypt/jobpost-key" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

# ============================================
# SECTION 4: Token Self-Management (Agent)
# ============================================
path "auth/token/lookup-self" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "auth/token/renew-self" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

⚙️ Appendix D: Vault Configuration Files — Production Templates

Three complete, annotated configuration files for production Vault deployments. Every stanza is explained with inline comments. Use these as your starting point for any Vault deployment — dev, staging, or production.

D.1 vault-config.hcl — Complete Production Server Config

/etc/vault.d/vault-config.hcl — Annotated Every Line
# ============================================================
# vault-config.hcl — Vault Production Server Configuration
# Path: /etc/vault.d/vault-config.hcl
# ============================================================

# ─── STORAGE: Integrated Raft (HA, no external deps) ───
storage "raft" {
  # Where Raft stores its data — use dedicated SSD/NVMe
  path = "/opt/vault/data"

  # Unique node ID — use hostname or K8s pod name
  node_id = "vault-node-1"          # vault-0, vault-1, vault-2 on K8s

  # Performance: batch writes for throughput (0=safe, 1-5=faster)
  performance_multiplier = 1        # 1 for SSD, 3 for NVMe

  # Max Raft log entry size (1MB default)
  max_entry_size = 1048576

  # ─── Cluster join (for nodes 2, 3, ...) ───
  retry_join {
    leader_api_addr = "https://vault-1.example.com:8200"
    leader_ca_cert_file = "/etc/vault.d/certs/ca.crt"
    leader_client_cert_file = "/etc/vault.d/certs/vault.crt"
    leader_client_key_file  = "/etc/vault.d/certs/vault.key"
  }
}

# ─── LISTENER: TCP with TLS ───
listener "tcp" {
  # Address: 0.0.0.0 binds all interfaces (use specific IP in prod)
  address     = "0.0.0.0:8200"       # Client API port
  cluster_address = "0.0.0.0:8201"   # Raft cluster port (private!)

  # TLS: MINIMUM 1.2 for production
  tls_cert_file = "/etc/vault.d/certs/vault.crt"
  tls_key_file  = "/etc/vault.d/certs/vault.key"
  tls_min_version = "tls12"

  # Performance tuning
  max_request_size     = 33554432     # 32MB max request body
  max_request_duration = "90s"        # Kill slow requests

  # Proxy headers (if behind load balancer)
  x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs = "10.0.0.0/8"
}

# ─── SEAL: Auto-Unseal via AWS KMS ───
seal "awskms" {
  region     = "us-east-1"
  kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abc-123-def"
  # Alternative: seal "transit" { ... } for Vault-to-Vault auto-unseal
  # Alternative: seal "pkcs11" { ... } for HSM-based auto-unseal
}

# ─── TELEMETRY: Prometheus Metrics ───
telemetry {
  prometheus_retention_time = "30s"   # How long to keep metrics
  disable_hostname          = true    # Use pod name in K8s, not hostname
}

# ─── API: Enable UI ───
ui = true                             # Web UI at :8200/ui

# ─── LEASE LIMITS: Global Safety Ceilings ───
max_lease_ttl     = "768h"            # 32 days — absolute maximum
default_lease_ttl = "768h"            # 32 days — default if not specified

# ─── PLUGINS: Custom engines/auth ───
plugin_directory = "/opt/vault/plugins"

# ─── LOG LEVEL ───
log_level = "info"                    # trace|debug|info|warn|error

D.2 vault-agent-config.hcl — Vault Agent Sidecar Configuration

vault-agent-config.hcl — For K8s Sidecar (anihpj/jobpost)
# ============================================================
# vault-agent-config.hcl — Vault Agent for anihpj/jobpost
# Used by: Vault Agent Injector (K8s mutating webhook)
# ============================================================

# ─── SECTION 1: Vault Server Connection ───
vault {
  # Vault server address (K8s service DNS)
  address = "https://vault.vault.svc:8200"

  # CA certificate for TLS verification
  ca_cert = "/vault/tls/ca.crt"

  # Retry settings if Vault is unreachable
  retry {
    num_retries = 12                 # Try 12 times before giving up
    retry_interval = "5s"           # Wait 5s between retries
  }
}

# ─── SECTION 2: Auto-Auth (How Agent Authenticates) ───
auto_auth {
  # Kubernetes auth — Agent uses pod's SA JWT
  method "kubernetes" {
    # Path where K8s auth is mounted in Vault
    mount_path = "auth/kubernetes"

    # Role name (must match vault write auth/kubernetes/role/...)
    role = "anihpj-app"

    # JWT path (auto-mounted by K8s)
    token_path = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"
  }

  # Where to store the Vault token AFTER authentication
  sink "file" {
    path = "/vault/.vault-token"    # Shared with templates
    mode = 0644
  }
}

# ─── SECTION 3: Cache — Reduces Vault API Load ───
cache {
  use_auto_auth_token = true         # Cache auto-auth tokens
  # Without cache: every secret read = Vault API call
  # With cache: first read = API call, subsequent = instant from memory
}

# ─── SECTION 4: Templates — Rendered Secret Files ───
template {
  # Source: inline Go template with Vault secret interpolation
  contents = <<-EOT
  {{- with secret "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost" -}}
  DB_HOST={{ .Data.data.db_host }}
  DB_PORT={{ .Data.data.db_port }}
  DB_NAME={{ .Data.data.db_name }}
  {{- end }}
  EOT

  # Destination: app reads this file for config
  destination = "/vault/secrets/database.env"

  # Signal app when secrets change (optional)
  command = "kill -HUP $(cat /vault/pid/app.pid)"
}

template {
  # Second template: dynamic DB credentials
  contents = <<-EOT
  {{- with secret "database/creds/jobpost-role" -}}
  DB_USER={{ .Data.username }}
  DB_PASS={{ .Data.password }}
  {{- end }}
  EOT
  destination = "/vault/secrets/db-creds.env"
}

# ─── SECTION 5: Listener (optional — for Agent API) ───
listener "tcp" {
  address     = "127.0.0.1:8100"
  tls_disable = true                 # Local only, no TLS needed
}
📋 Key Agent Config Notes
  • auto_auth: Defines HOW the Agent proves identity. K8s auth = pod's SA JWT. AppRole = RoleID+SecretID. AWS = EC2 instance identity.
  • template: Can have MULTIPLE template blocks — one per config file. Each template can fetch from multiple Vault paths.
  • cache: Reduces Vault API calls by 90%+. Secrets served from memory until TTL expires.
  • command: Executes AFTER template renders — signals app to reload config.
  • KV v2 note: Use .Data.data.key for KV v2, .Data.key for dynamic secrets!

D.3 vault-helm-values.yaml — Kubernetes HA Deployment (3-Node Raft)

values.yaml — Helm Chart for Production Vault on K8s
# ============================================================
# vault-helm-values.yaml — Production Vault on Kubernetes
# Deploy: helm install vault hashicorp/vault -f values.yaml
# ============================================================

# ─── GLOBAL ───
global:
  enabled: true
  tlsDisable: false                   # TLS REQUIRED for production

# ─── SERVER: HA Mode with Raft ───
server:
  # Number of Vault pods (odd number for Raft quorum)
  ha:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 3                       # 3 nodes minimum for HA
    raft:
      enabled: true                   # Integrated storage (no Consul needed)
      config: |
        ui = true
        listener "tcp" {
          tls_disable = false
          address     = "[::]:8200"
          cluster_address = "[::]:8201"
          tls_cert_file = "/vault/userconfig/tls/vault.crt"
          tls_key_file  = "/vault/userconfig/tls/vault.key"
        }
        storage "raft" {
          path = "/vault/data"
        }
        # Auto-unseal via Transit (or cloud KMS)
        # seal "awskms" { ... }

  # Pod resources (adjust for workload)
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: "512Mi"
      cpu: "250m"
    limits:
      memory: "2Gi"
      cpu: "1000m"

  # Affinity: spread pods across nodes for HA
  affinity: |
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: vault
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

  # Readiness probe: /v1/sys/health?standbyok=true
  readinessProbe:
    enabled: true
    path: "/v1/sys/health?standbyok=true"
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 5

  # Liveness probe: vault status via exec
  livenessProbe:
    enabled: true
    path: "/v1/sys/health?standbyok=true"
    initialDelaySeconds: 60

# ─── UI: Enable Vault Web UI ───
ui:
  enabled: true
  serviceType: "ClusterIP"
  # For external access, use Ingress or LoadBalancer

# ─── INJECTOR: Vault Agent Sidecar Injector ───
injector:
  enabled: true
  # Automatically injects Vault Agent into pods with annotations
  # Pod annotation: vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"

  # Injector resources
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: "256Mi"
      cpu: "100m"
    limits:
      memory: "512Mi"
      cpu: "500m"

# ─── CSI: Secrets Store CSI Driver ───
csi:
  enabled: true
  # Mount Vault secrets as K8s volumes
  # Pod annotation: vault.hashicorp.com/csi-volume: "secret-volume"

# ─── TLS: Certificate Configuration ───
# Generate certs: helm template → inject into values
# Or use cert-manager for automatic TLS
📋 Key Helm Values Notes
  • server.ha.replicas: MUST be odd (3, 5, 7). 3 is minimum for HA.
  • podAntiAffinity: Ensures pods run on different nodes — if a node fails, quorum survives.
  • injector.enabled: The mutating webhook that adds Vault Agent to pods automatically.
  • csi.enabled: Alternative to sidecar — mounts secrets as volumes without extra containers.
  • After deploy: kubectl exec vault-0 -- vault operator init → unseal all 3 pods → configure auth + secrets.

  name: anihpj-sa

k8s/deployment.yaml — Django + Vault Agent Sidecar
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jobpost
  namespace: anihpj
  labels:
    app: jobpost
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: jobpost
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: jobpost
      annotations:
        # ─── Vault Agent Sidecar Injector Annotations ───
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
        vault.hashicorp.com/role: "anihpj-app"
        # Inject database config from KV v2
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-db: "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost"
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-template-db: |
          {{- with secret "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost" -}}
          DB_HOST={{ .Data.data.db_host }}
          DB_PORT={{ .Data.data.db_port }}
          DB_NAME={{ .Data.data.db_name }}
          {{- end }}
        # Inject dynamic DB credentials
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-creds: "database/creds/jobpost-role"
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-template-creds: |
          {{- with secret "database/creds/jobpost-role" -}}
          DB_USER={{ .Data.username }}
          DB_PASS={{ .Data.password }}
          {{- end }}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: anihpj-sa  # Used by Vault K8s auth
      containers:
      - name: jobpost
        image: anihpj/jobpost:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: jobpost-secrets  # From VSO (optional fallback)
        volumeMounts:
        - name: vault-secrets
          mountPath: /vault/secrets
          readOnly: true
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
      volumes:
      - name: vault-secrets
        emptyDir: {}

G.3 Vault Configurations

vault/kv-setup.sh — Enable KV v2 + Write Secrets
#!/bin/bash
# vault/kv-setup.sh — KV v2 setup for anihpj/jobpost

# Enable KV v2 at path "secret" (default)
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2

# Write application configuration
vault kv put secret/anihpj/jobpost \
    db_host="postgres.anihpj.svc" \
    db_port="5432" \
    db_name="jobpost" \
    redis_host="redis.anihpj.svc" \
    redis_port="6379" \
    django_secret_key="super-secret-key-change-me" \
    email_host="smtp.anihpj.com" \
    email_port="587"

# Verify
vault kv get secret/anihpj/jobpost
vault/db-engine-setup.sh — DB Dynamic Secrets
#!/bin/bash
# vault/db-engine-setup.sh — Database engine for jobpost

# Enable database secrets engine
vault secrets enable database

# Configure PostgreSQL connection
vault write database/config/postgres \
    plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \
    allowed_roles="jobpost-role" \
    connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@postgres.anihpj.svc:5432/jobpost?sslmode=disable" \
    username="vault-admin" \
    password="vault-admin-pass-change-me"

# Create role with creation/revocation SQL
vault write database/roles/jobpost-role \
    db_name=postgres \
    creation_statements="CREATE USER \"{{name}}\" WITH PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}'; GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO \"{{name}}\";" \
    revocation_statements="REASSIGN OWNED BY \"{{name}}\" TO postgres; DROP OWNED BY \"{{name}}\"; DROP USER \"{{name}}\";" \
    default_ttl="1h" \
    max_ttl="24h"

# Test: generate credentials
vault read database/creds/jobpost-role
vault/policy-anihpj.hcl — ACL Policy
# vault/policy-anihpj.hcl
# Attached to K8s auth role "anihpj-app"
# This is what the jobpost Django app can access

# KV v2: Read application configuration
path "secret/data/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "secret/metadata/anihpj/jobpost/*" {
  capabilities = ["list"]
}

# Database: Generate dynamic credentials
path "database/creds/jobpost-role" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Token self-management (needed if token_no_default_policy=true)
path "auth/token/lookup-self" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "auth/token/renew-self" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
vault/k8s-auth-setup.sh — K8s Auth Method
#!/bin/bash
# vault/k8s-auth-setup.sh — Kubernetes auth for anihpj pods

# Enable Kubernetes auth
vault auth enable kubernetes

# Configure K8s auth (Vault inside cluster)
VAULT_SA_NAME=$(kubectl get sa vault -n vault -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}')
SA_JWT_TOKEN=$(kubectl get secret $VAULT_SA_NAME -n vault -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 --decode)
SA_CA_CRT=$(kubectl get secret $VAULT_SA_NAME -n vault -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 --decode)
K8S_HOST=$(kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}')

vault write auth/kubernetes/config \
    token_reviewer_jwt="$SA_JWT_TOKEN" \
    kubernetes_host="$K8S_HOST" \
    kubernetes_ca_cert="$SA_CA_CRT"

# Create role for anihpj/jobpost pods
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/anihpj-app \
    bound_service_account_names=anihpj-sa \
    bound_service_account_namespaces=anihpj \
    token_policies=anihpj-app \
    token_ttl=1h \
    token_max_ttl=4h

# Verify: write policy first, then test from a pod
vault policy write anihpj-app vault/policy-anihpj.hcl

G.4 Django Application

django/Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8000
# Vault Agent mounts secrets at /vault/secrets/
# Django reads from these files (via python-dotenv)
CMD ["gunicorn", "jobpost.wsgi:application", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000"]

G.5 Deployment Steps — End to End

1
Deploy Vault

Helm install 3-node HA

2
Init + Unseal

vault operator init + unseal ×3

3
Config Vault

KV + DB + Policy + K8s auth

4
Deploy anihpj

kubectl apply -f k8s/

5
Verify

Agent fetches secrets → Django starts

🔧 Quick Deploy Commands
# 1. Deploy Vault HA (3 nodes)
helm install vault hashicorp/vault -n vault --create-namespace \
    --set server.ha.enabled=true --set server.ha.replicas=3

# 2. Init + unseal all 3 pods
kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- vault operator init -key-shares=3 -key-threshold=2
kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- vault operator unseal <key1>
kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- vault operator unseal <key2>
# Repeat for vault-1 and vault-2...

# 3. Run Vault config scripts
./vault/kv-setup.sh
./vault/db-engine-setup.sh
./vault/k8s-auth-setup.sh

# 4. Deploy anihpj
kubectl apply -f k8s/
kubectl get pods -n anihpj
# Each pod has 2 containers: jobpost + vault-agent
