📖 Appendix H: Vault Glossary A-Z — 55 Key Terms

Every Vault term you'll encounter on the Associate exam — defined in plain English with chapter references for deeper study. Terms marked ⭐ are the most tested.

TermDefinitionSee
ACL Policy ⭐Access Control List policy written in HCL — controls what paths a token can access and with which capabilities. The #1 exam topic (28% of exam).Ch 12
AppRole ⭐Auth method for machines/apps — uses RoleID (public identifier) + SecretID (private credential). Most common machine auth. Supports response wrapping for secure SecretID delivery.Ch 7
Audit DeviceLogs all API requests/responses to a destination (file, socket, syslog). CRITICAL: if ALL audit devices fail to write, Vault stops ALL operations — this is a security feature called "default-deny".Ch 22
Auth MethodA way to authenticate to Vault: Token, AppRole, Kubernetes, JWT/OIDC, Userpass, LDAP, GitHub, cloud IAM. Each enabled at auth/<name> path.Ch 7
Auto-UnsealCloud KMS/HSM automatically decrypts the master key at startup — no manual unseal needed. Supported: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CKMS, Transit (secondary cluster).Ch 2
BackendLegacy term for "secrets engine" or "auth method". You'll still see it in older docs and CLI output. Modern docs use "secrets engine" and "auth method".Ch 4
BarrierCryptographic boundary — encrypts ALL data before it touches storage. The barrier key is encrypted by the master key. This is why even storage admins can't read Vault data.Ch 2
Batch Token ⭐Lightweight token type — NOT stored, NOT renewable, encrypted blob. Used for high-volume operations. Limited: no renewal, no orphan, no periodic, no children. Capped at ~100KB.Ch 10
Capability ⭐Action allowed on a path: create, read, update, delete, list, sudo, deny. deny ALWAYS wins against allow. sudo needed for root-protected paths.Ch 12
CSI ProviderContainer Storage Interface driver — mounts Vault secrets as K8s volumes. Pods read secrets from mounted files. Alternative to Vault Agent Injector sidecar.Ch 15
Database Engine ⭐Generates dynamic, short-lived database credentials. Flow: config → role → read creds. Auto-revokes on lease expiry. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Oracle, MSSQL, and more.Ch 5
DR ReplicationDisaster Recovery replication — creates a read-only standby cluster (Enterprise). In DR failover, promote secondary to primary. Separate from Performance replication.Ch 19
Dynamic Secret ⭐Generated on-demand with a lease. Auto-revoked when TTL expires. Each request gets unique credentials. Opposite of static secrets (shared, manual rotation).Ch 5
EntityUnified identity in Vault's identity system. One entity can have multiple aliases (e.g., same user authenticates via GitHub AND Userpass). Entities belong to groups.Ch 8
Expiration ManagerInternal Vault component that tracks ALL leases. When a lease's TTL expires, the expiration manager triggers revocation. Runs continuously in the background.Ch 5
GroupCollection of entities in the identity system. Groups can have policies attached — all member entities inherit them. Supports nested groups (Enterprise only).Ch 8
HCLHashiCorp Configuration Language — used for Vault policies and server configuration. Human-readable, JSON-compatible. Policy files use .hcl extension.Ch 12
IdentityVault's unified identity system. Components: Entities (users/machines), Groups (collections of entities), Aliases (entity's identity in a specific auth method).Ch 8
KV v1Simple key-value secrets engine — overwrite on write, no versioning. Path: secret/<key>. Simpler but less powerful than KV v2.Ch 4
KV v2 ⭐Versioned key-value store — keeps 10 versions by default. Path has /data/ for secrets and /metadata/ for version info. Supports patch (partial update), delete (soft), and destroy (permanent). #1 tested engine.Ch 4
Lease ⭐Time-bound credential with TTL. Expires unless renewed before TTL. Every dynamic secret has a lease. Lease ID format: <engine>/creds/<role>/<id>.Ch 5
Lease RenewalExtending a lease's TTL before it expires. Can be manual (vault lease renew) or automatic (periodic tokens with renewal). Can only renew to MaxTTL.Ch 5
MaxTTLMaximum total time a lease can exist. Even with renewal, a lease expires at MaxTTL. Set on role/token creation. Example: TTL=1h, MaxTTL=24h → renew 23 times max.Ch 5
mlockPrevents Vault process memory from swapping to disk — CRITICAL for security because master key and decrypted secrets are in memory. Requires CAP_IPC_LOCK on Linux.Ch 25
MountEnabling a secrets engine or auth method at a specific path. Example: vault secrets enable -path=anihpj kv-v2 mounts KV v2 at anihpj/.Ch 4
NamespaceIsolated tenant within a Vault cluster (Enterprise only). Each namespace has its own secrets engines, policies, tokens, and identity. Root namespace sees all children.Ch 24
Orphan Token ⭐Token with NO parent — survives parent token revocation. Created with -orphan flag. Periodic tokens are auto-orphaned. Important: orphan != root.Ch 10
Periodic Token ⭐Auto-renewing token within a "period". No max TTL — lives forever if renewed. Automatically orphaned. Used for long-running services and Vault Agent.Ch 10
Permanent TokenToken with NO TTL (TTL=0). Never expires. Rare — use with extreme caution. Root token is NOT permanent (has TTL unless explicitly set to 0).Ch 10
PKI Engine ⭐Generates X.509 certificates — Vault acts as internal Certificate Authority (CA). Flow: root CA → intermediate CA → issue certs. Auto-rotation of CAs. CRL support.Ch 6
PluginCustom Go binary that extends Vault — can be a secrets engine or auth method. Communicates via gRPC over localhost. Registered in plugin catalog with SHA256 checksum.Ch 26
Policy ⭐HCL document defining capabilities on paths. Attached to tokens. Format: path "secret/data/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }. Multiple policies merge (union of capabilities).Ch 12
Raft ⭐Integrated storage backend — the DEFAULT for new Vault installs. Provides High Availability via leader election. Has snapshot/restore. Requires odd number of nodes (3 or 5).Ch 2
Response WrappingSingle-use wrapping token containing a secret. The wrap token is consumed on first unwrap — provides secure, tamper-evident delivery. Used for SecretID distribution to apps.Ch 11
Root TokenAll-powerful token created at vault operator init. Bypasses ALL policies. Can do anything. Should be revoked after initial setup. NEVER used for day-to-day operations.Ch 10
Seal ⭐Encrypts the master key — Vault is locked ("sealed") until unsealed. On restart, Vault automatically seals. Unsealing requires key shares (Shamir) or auto-unseal via cloud KMS.Ch 2
Secret Engine ⭐Component that generates, stores, or encrypts secrets. Types: KV (static), Database (dynamic), PKI (certs), Transit (encryption-as-a-service), TOTP, SSH, and more.Ch 4
SecretIDPrivate half of AppRole authentication. Delivered securely via response wrapping. Can be time-limited and one-time-use. Together with RoleID, authenticates an application.Ch 7
SentinelPolicy-as-code framework for fine-grained access control (Enterprise only). Write rules like "deny access if request comes from outside 192.168.0.0/16". Much more powerful than ACL policies.Ch 24
Service Token ⭐Default token type — stored in Vault, renewable, supports parent-child hierarchy. Can create child tokens. Can be orphan or periodic. Most common token for applications.Ch 10
Shamir ⭐Secret sharing algorithm — splits the master key into N parts (shares), K needed to reconstruct (threshold). Example: 5 shares, 3 threshold. Mathematically secure — less than K shares reveals NOTHING.Ch 2
SnapshotPoint-in-time backup of Raft data. Created with vault operator raft snapshot save. Can be restored to a fresh cluster. Best practice: automate daily snapshots.Ch 18
SSH EngineGenerates one-time SSH passwords (OTP) or signed SSH certificates. Integrates with SSH CA. Avoids managing SSH keys manually.Ch 6
Static SecretPre-written secret in KV store. Shared among all consumers. Manual rotation. No lease, no auto-expiry. Example: API keys, config values that rarely change.Ch 4
sudoCapability required for root-protected paths (sys/mounts, sys/auth, sys/policy). Only root token and tokens with sudo capability can modify these paths.Ch 12
TelemetryRuntime metrics exposed for monitoring. Format: Prometheus or StatsD. Key metrics: vault_core_handle_request, vault_token_count, vault_expire_num_leases.Ch 23
Token ⭐Primary authentication credential in Vault. Attached policies determine access. Types: service (default), batch (lightweight). Properties: orphan, periodic, renewable, TTL, MaxTTL.Ch 10
TOTP EngineTime-Based One-Time Password generation. Vault generates TOTP codes — used for MFA/2FA. No external TOTP service needed.Ch 6
Transit Engine ⭐Encryption-as-a-Service — Vault encrypts your data but NEVER stores it. You keep the ciphertext. Supports key rotation (old key decrypts, new key encrypts), rewrap, HMAC, signing.Ch 20
TTL ⭐Time To Live — initial lease duration. After TTL, the lease/token expires unless renewed. Set per-role, per-token, or system-wide. Common values: 1h, 24h, 30d.Ch 5
Unseal ⭐Process of providing key shares to reconstruct the master key. After init, Vault is sealed. Unsealing makes it operational. vault operator unseal <key_share> — repeat until threshold met.Ch 2
Vault AgentSidecar process that auto-authenticates to Vault and renders secrets to files. Components: auto_auth (login), cache (reduce API calls), template (render secrets as config files).Ch 15
VSOVault Secrets Operator — Kubernetes operator that syncs Vault secrets to native K8s Secrets. Part of the Vault-K8s ecosystem. Different from Agent Injector and CSI.Ch 16
Wildcard (*)Policy path wildcard that matches any characters WITHIN a path segment. Example: secret/data/* matches secret/data/app but NOT secret/data/app/db. Use + or ** for multi-level.Ch 12
Wrap TokenSingle-use token for response wrapping — consumed on first unwrap. Provides tamper-evident, secure delivery of secrets. If intercepted, the intended recipient knows because the token won't unwrap.Ch 11

🔧 Appendix J: Troubleshooting Decision Trees — 10 Common Issues

10 decision trees for the most common Vault issues. Each follows the pattern: Symptom → Diagnostic Commands → Root Cause → Fix. Bookmark this for exam day and production incidents.

🔒 DT1: Vault Won't Unseal

Symptom: vault operator unseal fails or hangs

Diagnose:
vault status — check Sealed + Unseal Progress
vault operator init -status — check threshold

Root Causes:
• Wrong key share (typo or wrong share)
• Already unsealed (check status)
• Auto-unseal configured (no manual needed)
• Threshold not yet met (need 3 of 5 keys)

Fix: Verify key shares with key holders. Check vault status for progress. For auto-unseal, check KMS connectivity.

🎫 DT2: Token Authentication Fails

Symptom: permission denied or invalid token

Diagnose:
vault token lookup <token>
vault token capabilities <token> <path>

Root Causes:
• Token expired (TTL reached)
• Token revoked (parent revoked → tree)
• Policy doesn't grant access to path
• KV v2 needs /data/ prefix in policy path
• * doesn't span slashes

Fix: Create new token. Verify policies with vault token capabilities. Check KV v2 path has /data/. Use path "secret/data/*" not path "secret/*".

🗄️ DT3: Dynamic Secret Generation Fails

Symptom: vault read database/creds/role returns error

Diagnose:
vault read database/config/<name> — connection OK?
vault read database/roles/<role> — role exists?

Root Causes:
• Database unreachable (network, firewall)
• Root credentials expired/changed
• creation_statements SQL has syntax error
• Role TTL/max_ttl misconfigured
• Plugin not loaded

Fix: Test DB connection directly. Rotate root credentials: vault write database/rotate-root/<name>. Check PostgreSQL logs for SQL errors.

☸️ DT4: Kubernetes Auth Not Working

Symptom: Pod can't authenticate to Vault

Diagnose:
kubectl get sa <name> -n <ns> — SA exists?
vault read auth/kubernetes/config — config correct?
vault read auth/kubernetes/role/<name>

Root Causes:
• SA name/namespace mismatch in role binding
• JWT expired (K8s 1.22+: 1h default)
• token_reviewer_jwt expired
• Vault can't reach K8s API (network)
• Wrong audience in JWT

Fix: Verify bound_service_account_names matches SA. Check bound_service_account_namespaces. Update token_reviewer_jwt. Test from pod: vault write auth/kubernetes/login role=<name> jwt=@/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token

🌍 DT5: Replication Not Syncing

Symptom: Secondary cluster behind primary or sync errors

Diagnose:
vault read sys/replication/status
vault read sys/replication/dr/status

Root Causes:
• Network between primary and secondary down
• DR token expired (needs regeneration)
• Secondary sealed or restarted
• TLS certificate mismatch between clusters

Fix: Check network connectivity. Generate new DR token: vault write sys/replication/dr/secondary/generate-token. Re-enable on secondary with new token. Verify TLS certs match.

📝 DT6: Permission Denied in Audit Log

Symptom: Audit shows "error": "permission denied"

Diagnose:
vault token capabilities <token> <path>
cat audit.log | jq 'select(.error!="")'

Root Causes:
• Policy missing capability (need "read" not "list")
• KV v2 path missing /data/ prefix
• * wildcard doesn't span slashes
• deny capability overrides allow
• Token expired or revoked

Fix: Use vault token capabilities to test. Fix policy path: add /data/ for KV v2. Use ** for recursive matching. Check no deny policy is attached.

📡 DT7: Pod Can't Connect to Vault

Symptom: Connection timeout or refused from pod

Diagnose:
kubectl exec <pod> -- curl -k https://vault.vault:8200/v1/sys/health
kubectl get svc -n vault
kubectl get networkpolicy -n vault

Root Causes:
• Vault service DNS wrong (vault.vault vs vault.vault.svc)
• NetworkPolicy blocking pod→Vault traffic
• Vault pod not ready (sealed or crashing)
• TLS certificate not trusted by pod

Fix: Use full DNS: vault.vault.svc.cluster.local. Check NetworkPolicy allows ingress on 8200. Verify Vault is unsealed. Mount CA cert in pod.

🤖 DT8: Vault Agent Not Fetching Secrets

Symptom: Agent sidecar running but /vault/secrets/ empty

Diagnose:
kubectl logs <pod> -c vault-agent
kubectl describe pod <pod> — check annotations

Root Causes:
• Auth role doesn't match annotation
• SA not authorized in Vault role
• Template syntax error (missing .Data.data for KV v2)
• Vault unreachable from pod
• Token TTL too short

Fix: Verify vault.hashicorp.com/role matches Vault role name. Check SA in bound_service_account_names. Use .Data.data.key for KV v2 templates. Check Agent logs for specific error.

⚡ DT9: High API Latency

Symptom: Vault responses slow (>500ms p99)

Diagnose:
curl $VAULT_ADDR/v1/sys/metrics?format=prometheus | grep vault_core_handle_request
vault operator raft list-peers — check cluster health

Root Causes:
• Storage I/O bottleneck (HDD vs SSD)
• Too many active tokens (token count)
• Too many leases (lease count)
• Raft log too large (need snapshot)
• Network latency between Raft nodes

Fix: Use SSD/NVMe for Raft storage. Take Raft snapshot to compact log. Set performance_multiplier=1. Reduce token TTLs. Check inter-node network latency (<10ms).

🏥 DT10: Raft Cluster Unhealthy

Symptom: vault operator raft list-peers shows missing nodes or no leader

Diagnose:
vault operator raft list-peers
curl $VAULT_ADDR/v1/sys/leader
vault status — check HA status

Root Causes:
• 2 of 3 nodes failed (lost quorum)
• Network partition (split brain risk)
• Disk full on Raft nodes
• Node removed without proper decommission

Fix: Restore failed nodes. Remove permanently dead nodes: vault operator raft remove-peer <id>. For split brain: stop all nodes, restore from snapshot on one, rejoin others. Always deploy odd number of nodes. Monitor disk usage.

👥 POST /v1/identity/group
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/identity/group \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"name":"backend-team","member_entity_ids":["abc123..."],"policies":["backend-policy"]}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "id": "grp-789...",
    "name": "backend-team",
    "member_entity_ids": ["abc123..."],
    "policies": ["backend-policy"]
  }
}
🔗 POST /v1/identity/entity-alias
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/identity/entity-alias \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"name":"john-gh","canonical_id":"abc123...","mount_accessor":"auth_github_xxx"}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "id": "alias-uuid...",
    "name": "john-gh",
    "canonical_id": "abc123...",
    "mount_accessor": "auth_github_xxx"
  }
}
📋 LIST /v1/identity/entity/id
curl -s -X LIST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/identity/entity/id \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "keys": [
      "abc123-456-def",
      "ghi789-012-jkl",
      "mno345-678-pqr"
    ]
  }
}

K.4 — Secrets APIs: /secret/* (KV v2 — CRUD + Metadata + Destroy)

📝 POST /v1/secret/data/<path> (Create/Update)
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/data/anihpj/db \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"data":{"username":"jobpost","password":"s3cr3t!Abc"}}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "created_time": "2025-06-12T11:00:00Z",
    "custom_metadata": null,
    "deletion_time": "",
    "destroyed": false,
    "version": 3
  }
}
📖 GET /v1/secret/data/<path> (Read)
curl -s $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/data/anihpj/db \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "data": {
      "password": "s3cr3t!Abc",
      "username": "jobpost"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "created_time": "2025-06-12T11:00:00Z",
      "custom_metadata": null,
      "deletion_time": "",
      "destroyed": false,
      "version": 3
    }
  }
}

Note: .data.data (nested) for KV v2!

📋 LIST /v1/secret/metadata/<path>
curl -s -X LIST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/metadata/anihpj \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "keys": ["db", "api-keys", "ssl-certs"]
  }
}
🗑️ DELETE /v1/secret/data/<path> + Destroy
# Soft delete (creates new version = deletion marker)
curl -s -X DELETE $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/data/anihpj/db \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN"

# Permanent destroy (removes version)
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/destroy/anihpj/db \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"versions":[3]}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "destroyed": true,
    "deletion_time": "2025-06-12T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
🔧 PATCH /v1/secret/data/<path> (Partial Update)
curl -s -X PATCH $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/data/anihpj/db \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"data":{"password":"newpass!Xyz"}}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "created_time": "2025-06-12T12:05:00Z",
    "version": 4
  }
}
// .data.data.password = "newpass!Xyz"
// .data.data.username = "jobpost" (unchanged)

⚙️ POST /v1/database/config/<name>

    "plugin_name":"postgresql-database-plugin",

// HTTP 204 No Content (success)

// HTTP 204 No Content (success)

📜 POST /v1/pki/root/generate/<type>

}

K.7 — Transit Secrets Engine APIs (Encrypt, Decrypt, HMAC, Rotate)

🔐 POST /v1/transit/encrypt/<key>
BASE64=$(echo -n '{"db_pass":"s3cr3t"}' | base64)
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/transit/encrypt/jobpost-key \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d "{\"plaintext\":\"$BASE64\"}" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "ciphertext": "vault:v1:ABCDEF1234567890...",
    "key_version": 1
  }
}
🔓 POST /v1/transit/decrypt/<key>
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/transit/decrypt/jobpost-key \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"ciphertext":"vault:v1:ABCDEF1234567890..."}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "plaintext": "eyJkYl9wYXNzIjoiczNjcjN0In0="
  }
}
# Decode: echo "eyJ..." | base64 -d
# → {"db_pass":"s3cr3t"}
🔏 POST /v1/transit/hmac/<key>
BASE64=$(echo -n 'unique-data-value' | base64)
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/transit/hmac/jobpost-key \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d "{\"input\":\"$BASE64\"}" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "hmac": "vault:v1:Z29vZCBtb3JuaW5n..."
  }
}
🔄 POST /v1/transit/keys/<key>/rotate
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/transit/keys/jobpost-key/rotate \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "name": "jobpost-key",
    "latest_version": 2,
    "min_encryption_version": 1,
    "min_decryption_version": 1
  }
}
🔁 POST /v1/transit/rewrap/<key>
curl -s -X POST $VAULT_ADDR/v1/transit/rewrap/jobpost-key \
  -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"ciphertext":"vault:v1:OLD_ENCRYPTION..."}' | jq

Expected:

{
  "data": {
    "ciphertext": "vault:v2:NEW_ENCRYPTION...",
    "key_version": 2
  }
}

📋 K.8 — API Quick-Reference Cheat Sheet (One-Liner Summary)

💡 Exam Pro-Tip: Every Vault CLI command can be traced to an API call. Add -output-curl-string to any Vault CLI command to see the equivalent curl!

CategoryMethod + EndpointPurposeKey Response Field
HealthGET /v1/sys/healthCluster health.sealed, .initialized
InitPUT /v1/sys/initInitialize Vault.root_token, .keys[]
UnsealPUT /v1/sys/unsealSubmit key share.sealed, .progress
LeaderGET /v1/sys/leaderWhich node is active.is_self, .leader_address
Seal StatusGET /v1/sys/seal-statusSeal details.t, .n, .type
MetricsGET /v1/sys/metricsPrometheus metricsvault_core_*
Create TokenPOST /v1/auth/token/createIssue token.auth.client_token
Lookup TokenPOST /v1/auth/token/lookupInspect token.data.policies[]
Renew TokenPOST /v1/auth/token/renewExtend TTL.auth.lease_duration
Revoke TokenPOST /v1/auth/token/revokeInvalidate tokenHTTP 204
AppRole LoginPOST /v1/auth/approle/loginRoleID+SecretID.auth.client_token
K8s LoginPOST /v1/auth/kubernetes/loginSA JWT auth.auth.client_token
Create EntityPOST /v1/identity/entityIdentity entity.data.id
Create GroupPOST /v1/identity/groupIdentity group.data.id
KV PutPOST /v1/secret/data/<path>Write secret.data.version
KV GetGET /v1/secret/data/<path>Read secret.data.data ⚠️
KV ListLIST /v1/secret/metadata/<path>List keys.data.keys[]
KV DestroyPOST /v1/secret/destroy/<path>Permanent delete.data.destroyed
DB ConfigPOST /v1/database/config/<name>Configure DB engineHTTP 204
DB RolePOST /v1/database/roles/<name>Create DB roleHTTP 204
DB CredsGET /v1/database/creds/<role>Get dynamic creds.data.username, .data.password
PKI RootPOST /v1/pki/root/generate/internalGenerate root CA.data.certificate
PKI IssuePOST /v1/pki/issue/<role>Issue cert.data.certificate, .data.private_key
Transit EncryptPOST /v1/transit/encrypt/<key>Encrypt data.data.ciphertext
Transit DecryptPOST /v1/transit/decrypt/<key>Decrypt data.data.plaintext
Transit HMACPOST /v1/transit/hmac/<key>HMAC data.data.hmac
Transit RotatePOST /v1/transit/keys/<key>/rotateRotate key version.data.latest_version

🔐 Appendix N: Vault Authorship Certification Bridge — Custom Plugin Development with Go SDK

The HashiCorp Vault Authorship Certification validates your ability to build custom Vault plugins — both auth methods and secrets engines — using the official Go SDK. This appendix bridges Associate-level knowledge to Authorship-level expertise. You'll learn plugin architecture, registration, testing, debugging, and distribution.

🏗️ N.1 — Vault Plugin Architecture Overview

🛠️ N.3 — Building a Custom Secrets Engine: Scaffold

💡 Go SDK Import Path: github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk — This is the core SDK for all Vault plugins. Requires Go 1.21+.

📦 File Structure
vault-plugin-secrets-myengine/
├── main.go              # Entry point
├── backend.go           # Backend struct + Factory
├── path_config.go       # /config endpoint
├── path_creds.go        # /creds/:name endpoint
├── path_rotate.go       # /rotate/:name endpoint

📝 main.go — Entry Point
package main

import (
    "os"
    "github.com/hashicorp/go-hclog"
    "vault-plugin-secrets-myengine"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/api"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/plugin"
)

func main() {
    apiClientMeta := &api.PluginAPIClientMeta{}
    flags := apiClientMeta.FlagSet()
    flags.Parse(os.Args[1:])

    tlsConfig := apiClientMeta.GetTLSConfig()
    tlsProviderFunc := api.VaultPluginTLSProvider(tlsConfig)

    err := plugin.Serve(&plugin.ServeOpts{
        BackendFactoryFunc: myengine.Factory,
        TLSProviderFunc:    tlsProviderFunc,
    })
    if err != nil {
        logger := hclog.New(&hclog.LoggerOptions{})
        logger.Error("plugin shutting down", "error", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
}

🏭 N.4 — Backend Factory, Schema, and Path Definition

⚙️ backend.go — Factory + Backend
package myengine

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/framework"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/logical"
)

// Factory returns a new backend as logical.Backend
func Factory(ctx context.Context, conf *logical.BackendConfig) (
    logical.Backend, error) {
    b := backend()
    if err := b.Setup(ctx, conf); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return b, nil
}

type myBackend struct {
    *framework.Backend
}

func backend() *myBackend {
    b := &myBackend{}

    b.Backend = &framework.Backend{
        Help:        "MyEngine — Custom Secrets Engine",
        Paths:       b.paths(),    // Register all paths
        Secrets:     []*framework.Secret{
            b.credentialSecret(),
        },
        BackendType: logical.TypeLogical,
    }
    return b
}
🗂️ path_config.go — Config CRUD
package myengine

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/framework"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/logical"
)

func (b *myBackend) pathConfig() *framework.Path {
    return &framework.Path{
        Pattern: "config",
        Fields: map[string]*framework.FieldSchema{
            "api_key": {
                Type:        framework.TypeString,
                Description: "API key for external service",
                Required:    true,
            },
            "ttl": {
                Type:        framework.TypeDurationSecond,
                Description: "Default TTL for credentials",
                Default:     3600,
            },
        },
        Operations: map[logical.Operation]framework.OperationHandler{
            logical.ReadOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathConfigRead,
            },
            logical.CreateOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathConfigWrite,
            },
            logical.UpdateOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathConfigWrite,
            },
            logical.DeleteOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathConfigDelete,
            },
        },
        HelpSynopsis:    "Configure the MyEngine secrets engine",
        HelpDescription: "Set API key and default TTL for external service",
    }
}

func (b *myBackend) pathConfigWrite(ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    config := map[string]interface{}{
        "api_key": data.Get("api_key").(string),
        "ttl":     data.Get("ttl").(int),
    }

    entry, err := logical.StorageEntryJSON("config", config)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if err := req.Storage.Put(ctx, entry); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return nil, nil  // No response body = success
}

func (b *myBackend) pathConfigRead(ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    entry, err := req.Storage.Get(ctx, "config")
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if entry == nil {
        return logical.ErrorResponse("config not set"), nil
    }

    var config map[string]interface{}
    if err := entry.DecodeJSON(&config); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    // Don't return api_key in plaintext for security
    delete(config, "api_key")

    return &logical.Response{Data: config}, nil
}

🔑 N.5 — Dynamic Credentials: The Core Pattern

📝 path_creds.go — Read Operation
func (b *myBackend) pathCreds() *framework.Path {
    return &framework.Path{
        Pattern: "creds/" + framework.GenericNameRegex("name"),
        Fields: map[string]*framework.FieldSchema{
            "name": {
                Type:        framework.TypeString,
                Description: "Credential set name",
                Required:    true,
            },
        },
        Operations: map[logical.Operation]framework.OperationHandler{
            logical.ReadOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathCredsRead,
            },
        },
        HelpSynopsis: "Generate dynamic credentials",
    }
}

func (b *myBackend) pathCredsRead(ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    name := data.Get("name").(string)

    // 1. Read config
    config, err := b.readConfig(ctx, req.Storage)
    if err != nil || config == nil {
        return logical.ErrorResponse(
            "config not set"), nil
    }

    // 2. Call external API to create credentials
    username, password, err := b.createExternalCredential(
        ctx, config["api_key"].(string), name)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    // 3. Return with lease (auto-revocation!)
    resp := b.Secret(credentialType).Response(map[string]interface{}{
        "username": username,
        "password": password,
    }, map[string]interface{}{
        "cred_name": name,
    })

    resp.Secret.TTL = time.Duration(
        config["ttl"].(int)) * time.Second
    resp.Secret.MaxTTL = resp.Secret.TTL * 2

    return resp, nil
}
🔄 Revocation Handler
// Secret type definition
const credentialType = "myengine_credentials"

func (b *myBackend) credentialSecret() *framework.Secret {
    return &framework.Secret{
        Type: credentialType,
        Revoke: b.credentialRevoke,
        Renew:  b.credentialRenew,
    }
}

func (b *myBackend) credentialRevoke(ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    // InternalData is the metadata we stored
    credName := req.Secret.InternalData["cred_name"].(string)

    // Read config to get API key
    config, err := b.readConfig(ctx, req.Storage)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    // Call external API to delete the credential
    err = b.deleteExternalCredential(ctx,
        config["api_key"].(string), credName)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return nil, nil
}

// Renew: extend the lease without creating new creds
func (b *myBackend) credentialRenew(ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    config, _ := b.readConfig(ctx, req.Storage)
    ttl := time.Duration(config["ttl"].(int)) * time.Second

    resp := &logical.Response{Secret: req.Secret}
    resp.Secret.TTL = ttl
    resp.Secret.MaxTTL = ttl * 2
    return resp, nil
}

📋 N.6 — Registering All Paths

// paths() — register ALL endpoints the backend handles
func (b *myBackend) paths() []*framework.Path {
    return []*framework.Path{
        b.pathConfig(),       // /config           — CRUD
        b.pathCreds(),        // /creds/:name      — READ (dynamic)
        b.pathRotate(),       // /rotate/:name     — UPDATE
        b.pathListCreds(),    // /creds            — LIST
        b.pathInfo(),         // /info             — READ (health)
    }
}

// pathListCreds — LIST all credential sets
func (b *myBackend) pathListCreds() *framework.Path {
    return &framework.Path{
        Pattern: "creds/?",
        Operations: map[logical.Operation]framework.OperationHandler{
            logical.ListOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathCredsList,
            },
        },
        HelpSynopsis: "List all credential sets",
    }
}

📥 N.7 — Registering, Enabling, and Reloading Plugins

1️⃣ Build the Binary
# Build for Vault server's OS/arch
GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o \
  vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  ./main.go

# Calculate SHA256 (REQUIRED for registration)
sha256sum vault-plugin-secrets-myengine
# → abc123def456...89
2️⃣ Place & Register
# Copy to Vault plugin directory
cp vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  /etc/vault.d/plugins/

# Register in Vault's plugin catalog
vault plugin register \
  -sha256=abc123def456...89 \
  -command=vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  secret myengine
3️⃣ Enable the Engine
# Enable the secrets engine at a path
vault secrets enable \
  -path=myengine \
  -plugin-name=myengine \
  plugin

# Verify it's enabled
vault secrets list | grep myengine
# myengine/  plugin  plugin_abc123...  n/a
4️⃣ Reload After Changes
# Rebuild binary
go build -o vault-plugin-secrets-myengine

# Copy new binary over old
cp vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  /etc/vault.d/plugins/

# Get new SHA256
NEW_SHA=$(sha256sum \
  vault-plugin-secrets-myengine | cut -d' ' -f1)

# Reload plugin (hot reload — no downtime!)
vault plugin reload \
  -plugin myengine \
  -sha256=$NEW_SHA

🎫 N.8 — Building a Custom Auth Method Plugin

⚠️ Key Difference: Auth method plugins implement logical.AuthMethod (not logical.Backend). The Login() method is the most critical — it authenticates and returns a Vault token.

🔑 Login Handler — The Core
func (b *myAuthBackend) pathLogin() *framework.Path {
    return &framework.Path{
        Pattern: "login$",
        Fields: map[string]*framework.FieldSchema{
            "token": {
                Type:        framework.TypeString,
                Description: "External auth token",
                Required:    true,
            },
        },
        Operations: map[logical.Operation]framework.OperationHandler{
            logical.UpdateOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathLoginHandler,
            },
            logical.CreateOperation: &framework.PathOperation{
                Callback: b.pathLoginHandler,
            },
        },
        HelpSynopsis: "Authenticate with external token",
    }
}

func (b *myAuthBackend) pathLoginHandler(
    ctx context.Context,
    req *logical.Request,
    data *framework.FieldData) (
    *logical.Response, error) {

    extToken := data.Get("token").(string)

    // 1. Validate external token
    user, err := b.validateExternalToken(ctx, extToken)
    if err != nil {
        return logical.ErrorResponse(
            "invalid token: %v", err), nil
    }

    // 2. Build auth response with Vault token
    auth := &logical.Auth{
        Policies: user.Policies,
        Metadata: map[string]string{
            "username":   user.Username,
            "user_id":    user.ID,
            "auth_method": "my_custom_auth",
        },
        DisplayName: user.Username,
        LeaseOptions: logical.LeaseOptions{
            TTL:     1 * time.Hour,
            MaxTTL:  24 * time.Hour,
            Renewable: true,
        },
        Alias: &logical.Alias{
            Name:     user.Username,
            Metadata: map[string]string{
                "user_id": user.ID,
            },
        },
        InternalData: map[string]interface{}{
            "external_token": extToken,
        },
    }

    return &logical.Response{
        Auth: auth,
    }, nil
}
📝 Factory for Auth Plugin
// AuthMethod factory — returns AuthMethod interface
func Factory(ctx context.Context,
    conf *logical.BackendConfig) (
    logical.Backend, error) {

    b := &myAuthBackend{}
    b.Backend = &framework.Backend{
        Help: "MyCustomAuth — External token auth",
        Paths: []*framework.Path{
            b.pathLogin(),
            b.pathConfig(),
            b.pathRole(),
            b.pathListRoles(),
        },
        AuthRenew: b.pathLoginRenew,
        BackendType: logical.TypeCredential,
    }
    return b, nil
}

// Register as AUTH plugin (not SECRET plugin)
// vault plugin register -sha256=... \
//   -command=vault-plugin-auth-mycustom \
//   auth mycustom
//
// vault auth enable \
//   -path=mycustom \
//   -plugin-name=mycustom plugin

🧪 N.9 — Testing Plugins (Unit + Acceptance)

✅ Unit Tests with Mock Storage
import (
    "testing"
    "github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/logical"
)

func TestConfigWriteRead(t *testing.T) {
    // Create in-memory test backend
    b, storage := getTestBackend(t)

    // Test config write
    req := &logical.Request{
        Operation: logical.UpdateOperation,
        Path:      "config",
        Storage:   storage,
        Data: map[string]interface{}{
            "api_key": "test-key-123",
            "ttl":     7200,
        },
    }
    resp, err := b.HandleRequest(ctx, req)
    if err != nil || resp != nil {
        t.Fatalf("write failed: %v", err)
    }

    // Test config read
    req.Operation = logical.ReadOperation
    req.Data = nil
    resp, err = b.HandleRequest(ctx, req)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("read failed: %v", err)
    }
    if resp.Data["ttl"] != 7200 {
        t.Fatalf("expected ttl=7200, got %v",
            resp.Data["ttl"])
    }
}

func getTestBackend(t *testing.T) (
    logical.Backend, logical.Storage) {
    config := &logical.BackendConfig{
        Logger:      hclog.NewNullLogger(),
        System:      &logical.StaticSystemView{},
        StorageView: &logical.InmemStorage{},
    }
    b, err := Factory(ctx, config)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("factory failed: %v", err)
    }
    return b, config.StorageView
}
🔬 Acceptance Tests with Real Vault
// acceptance_test.go — requires VAULT_ACC=1
func TestAcceptanceFullFlow(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("VAULT_ACC") == "" {
        t.Skip("set VAULT_ACC=1 for acceptance tests")
    }

    cluster := vault.NewTestCluster(t,
        &vault.CoreConfig{
            LogicalBackends: map[string]logical.Factory{
                "myengine": Factory,
            },
        },
        &vault.TestClusterOptions{
            HandlerFunc: vaulthttp.Handler,
        })
    defer cluster.Cleanup()

    client := cluster.Cores[0].Client

    // Enable the plugin
    err := client.Sys().Mount("myengine",
        &api.MountInput{
            Type: "myengine",
        })
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Write config
    _, err = client.Logical().Write(
        "myengine/config",
        map[string]interface{}{
            "api_key": "test-key",
            "ttl":     3600,
        })
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Read credentials
    resp, err := client.Logical().Read(
        "myengine/creds/test-user")
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if resp.Data["username"] == "" {
        t.Fatal("expected username")
    }
}

🐛 N.10 — Debugging & Troubleshooting Plugins

📋 Plugin Status Check
# List all registered plugins
vault plugin list secret
vault plugin list auth

# Check plugin info (SHA, version, type)
vault plugin info secret myengine

# Check if plugin is running
ps aux | grep vault-plugin-secrets
📝 Vault Server Logs
# Check Vault logs for plugin errors
journalctl -u vault -f | grep plugin

# Common log messages:
# "plugin exited" — plugin crashed
# "plugin not found" — binary missing
# "SHA256 mismatch" — rebuild & re-register
# "gRPC connection refused" — TLS mismatch
🔍 Runtime Debug with dlv
# Compile with debug symbols
go build -gcflags="all=-N -l" \
  -o vault-plugin-secrets-myengine

# Attach debugger to plugin PID
dlv attach $(pgrep -f myengine)

# Set breakpoint
(dlv) break pathCredsRead
(dlv) continue
🔄 Force Reload Debug Workflow
# 1. Rebuild
go build -o vault-plugin-secrets-myengine

# 2. Move to plugins dir
cp vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  /etc/vault.d/plugins/

# 3. Get new checksum
NEW_SHA=$(sha256sum \
  vault-plugin-secrets-myengine | \
  cut -d' ' -f1)

# 4. Reload (hot — keeps existing leases)
vault plugin reload \
  -plugin myengine -sha256=$NEW_SHA

# 5. Test immediately
vault read myengine/info

🛡️ N.11 — Plugin Security Best Practices

#PracticeDescriptionWhy It Matters
1🔒 Mutual TLSEnable mTLS between Vault and pluginPrevents unauthorized plugin impersonation
2📦 SHA256 VerificationAlways register with exact binary hashPrevents tampered binaries from loading
3🔑 Least PrivilegePlugin runs as dedicated OS user with minimal permissionsLimits blast radius if plugin is compromised
4📝 Audit All OperationsLog every credential creation/revocationEssential for compliance and forensics
5🚫 No Secrets in LogsNever log sensitive values (passwords, tokens, keys)Prevents secret leakage via log files
6⏱️ Always Set TTLsEvery secret must have TTL and MaxTTLEnsures auto-revocation; prevents orphaned creds
7🔄 Always Implement RevokeEvery secret type must have a Revoke handlerWithout this, dynamic creds can never be cleaned up
8🧪 Test RevocationWrite acceptance tests that verify credential revocationEnsures cleanup works before production deployment
9🗂️ Isolate StorageUse req.Storage prefix scoped to your plugin mountPrevents cross-plugin data access
10📦 Dependency AuditRegularly scan Go dependencies with govulncheckPrevents supply chain vulnerabilities

📋 Plugin Metadata
// In your Makefile
VERSION ?= 1.0.0
BUILD_DATE ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
GIT_COMMIT ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD)

build:
  go build -ldflags "\
    -X main.Version=$(VERSION) \
    -X main.BuildDate=$(BUILD_DATE) \
    -X main.GitCommit=$(GIT_COMMIT)" \
    -o vault-plugin-secrets-myengine

# Create GitHub release
release: build
  GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o \
    dist/vault-plugin-secrets-myengine-linux-amd64
  GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 go build -o \
    dist/vault-plugin-secrets-myengine-darwin-amd64
  GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -o \
    dist/vault-plugin-secrets-myengine-windows-amd64.exe
  cd dist && sha256sum * > SHA256SUMS
📖 Installation README
# vault-plugin-secrets-myengine

Custom Vault secrets engine for MyService.

## Quick Start
```bash
# 1. Download
wget https://github.com/org/myengine/releases/\
  download/v1.0.0/\
  vault-plugin-secrets-myengine-linux-amd64

# 2. Verify
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 3. Install
cp vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  /etc/vault.d/plugins/

# 4. Register
vault plugin register \
  -sha256=$(sha256sum ... | cut -d' ' -f1) \
  -command=vault-plugin-secrets-myengine \
  secret myengine

# 5. Enable
vault secrets enable \
  -path=myengine \
  -plugin-name=myengine plugin

# 6. Configure
vault write myengine/config \
  api_key="your-api-key" ttl=3600

# 7. Get credentials
vault read myengine/creds/my-app
```
